# localmelo

> localmelo is a local personal agent that runs tasks with tools (shell, Python, files, MCP servers) and memory on a model server the user runs (oMLX, Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible server) or on a cloud API (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, NVIDIA). It offers the `melo` command, which returns a fixed exit code per run and prints one JSON line with `--output-format json`, an experimental Python API, and an HTTP gateway on 127.0.0.1. It is pre-alpha: interfaces may change before v0.1.0.

- Command words (only as the first argument, exact match; a task that starts with one is quoted or follows `--`; one command word after options and no `--` exits 2, saying where it goes): `melo setup` = `--reconfigure`, `melo serve [-p N] [--host H] [--force]` = `--serve [--port N] [--host H] [--allow-unconfigured]` (`--enable-playground` is still accepted: it does nothing and prints that it was removed), `melo serve install|uninstall|status|stop` = `--daemon ACTION` (`stop`: SIGTERM to the gateway the endpoint file names, up to 10 s; `Stopped the gateway on port N.`, `No gateway is running.`, exit 1 when it did not stop), `melo console [--reset]` = `--gateway-login` / `--gateway-rotate-token` (at a local terminal `melo serve` and `melo console` open the web console in the browser, signed in; over SSH, or when no browser starts, `melo console` prints a one-use link, exits 2 when stdout is not a terminal and 1 when no gateway listens), `melo worker BRIEF [--parent ID] [--title T]` = `--brief BRIEF [--parent-run ID] [--save-session T]`, `melo import FORMAT FILE` = `--import-session FORMAT FILE`, `melo task VERB` = `melo-task VERB`, `melo config` shows the config file and what differs from the defaults. Letters and short names: `-m/--model` = `--chat-model`, `-u/--url` = `--base-url`, `-s/--steps` = `--max-steps`, `-o/--output` = `--output-format`, `--mcp` = `--mcp-config`, `-w` = `--workspace`, `-t` = `--timeout`, `-y` = `--yolo`, `-V` = `--version`; `--title T` = `--save-session T`. Every old spelling keeps working and parses to the same result (launchers, the benchmark and the macOS app need no change). `melo -h` is 23 lines (the everyday options and `setup`, `serve`, `console` with what each does); `melo -h all` (also plain `-h` with `[ui] mode = "developer"` or `--developer`) lists every option, command and setting; `melo COMMAND -h` explains one command. Table: [Command-line reference](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/cli.md#old-spelling-to-new). Tiers: [Command-line reference](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/cli.md#default-and-developer-mode).
- Settings: `-X KEY=VALUE` (or `--set KEY=VALUE`, repeatable, before `--`) changes one `config.toml` key for one run and never writes the file; KEY is `section.name` (`retrieval.k`; `request_timeout_s` has no section), the value is TOML (`true`, `5`, `"v3"`) else text, and `on`/`off` mean booleans. A key with an old option becomes that option before parsing (`-X retrieval.k=5` = `--recall-k 5`, same checks and requests); another key (`cli.stream`, `scheduler.policy`) overrides the loaded config; a bad value or unknown key exits 2 (an unknown key that is an option's name gets the option: `agent.max_steps` is `-s N (--steps)`). `melo config keys [FILTER]`, `melo config get KEY` and `melo config set KEY VALUE` list, read and save keys; nine keys are for one run only (`agent.attempt_policy`, `agent.reflection_gate`, `agent.tool_exposure`, `memory.dir`, `memory.keep_decision_text`, `retrieval.extra_body`, `endpoint.embedding_url`, `endpoint.embedding_model`, `endpoint.reasoning_field`). Old option = key: `--attempt-policy` = `agent.attempt_policy`; `--reflection-gate` = `agent.reflection_gate`; `--fixed-prefix` = `agent.fixed_prefix`; `--window-eviction` = `agent.window_eviction`; `--reflect-tool-guard` = `agent.reflect_tool_guard`; `--cache-layout` = `agent.cache_layout`; `--window-messages` = `agent.window_messages`; `--brief-items` = `agent.brief_items`; `--reasoning` = `agent.reasoning`; `--replay-turns` = `agent.replay_turns`; `--note-writer` = `agent.note_writer`; `--captured-history` = `agent.captured_history`; `--context-window` = `agent.context_window`; `--output-reserve` = `agent.output_reserve`; `--safety-margin` = `agent.safety_margin`; `--tool-exposure` = `agent.tool_exposure`; `--retriever` = `retrieval.retriever`; `--recall-at` = `retrieval.recall_at`; `--recall-k` = `retrieval.k`; `--recall-kinds` = `retrieval.kinds`; `--recall-placement` = `retrieval.placement`; `--recall-min-score` = `retrieval.min_score`; `--retrieval-extra-body` = `retrieval.extra_body`; `--admit-on-outcome` = `memory.admit_on_outcome`; `--keep-decision-text` = `memory.keep_decision_text`; `--memory-dir` = `memory.dir`; `--request-timeout` = `request_timeout_s`; `--no-save-session` = `sessions.record_direct`; `--embedding-base-url` = `endpoint.embedding_url`; `--embedding-model` = `endpoint.embedding_model`; `--reasoning-field` = `endpoint.reasoning_field`. Table: [Settings](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/cli.md#settings).
- Config file: `save()` writes only keys that differ from their default (plus `chat_backend` and `embedding_backend`; an all-default backend table is left out). A value of the wrong kind (`port = "8401"`) is a configuration error in one sentence (`[gateway] port must be a whole number, got '8401'`, exit 1), never a traceback. Text in local and cloud backend tables loses spaces at both ends on read and on Settings save (`api_key` stays as typed).
- Backends are rows of data in `support/backends/openai_family.py` (`LOCAL_SERVERS`; hosted services are `support/hosted.py` presets): `LOCAL_BACKENDS` and `CLOUD_BACKENDS` are their keys and every list of backends derives from them; `GET /api/health` `model.local` says whether the chat backend is the user's own server. A new backend is one row plus a `Config` field named by its key.
- Website and README commands are generated terminal blocks: edit `scripts/usage_blocks.toml`, run `uv run python scripts/usage_blocks.py sync` (`--check` fails when a `<!-- usage:ID -->` region or `docs/assets/usage/*.svg` is stale); Markdown fences tagged `shell` or `console` render as the same blocks in `scripts/build_docs.py`; a block's `mode` can also be `chat` (messages typed into melo's own chat, marked `›`).
- Install from a clone named `localmelo` with Python 3.11+: `uv sync --extra gateway`, then run `uv run melo` in the clone (`melo` is not on PATH). MIT license. localmelo never downloads, starts or serves models.
- Read-only server setup preview (`support/server_setup/plan.py`): no saved backend + no server found gives at most six summary lines; saved backend + none found retains the full setup menu. Supported Macs show the recommendation (oMLX 0.7.3 + `mlx-community/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-4bit` @ `50d427756c6b1b2fe0c0a10f67fbda1fc8e82c1b`, 2278972236 model bytes) and the download upper bound, plus one RAM warning below 16 GB or when unknown; other systems get manual guidance. The summary prints once; the list offers Check again / `Show how to set one up` (at most six numbered steps) / Enter an address / Quit. Intro precedes discovery; an exception while reading the platform keeps manual guidance. Pipes/TERM=dumb get a guide link, retaining Enter/address/q. Cache: HF_HUB_CACHE > HUGGINGFACE_HUB_CACHE > HF_HOME/hub > XDG/default; state: ~/.cache/localmelo/server-setup/omlx-<version>. Automatic setup is "coming soon"; nothing installs/downloads/starts/saves/binds. Manual servers need manual stop; the steps use port 49152 as an example. Direct `--base-url` and configured/web/app connections unchanged. [Setup preview](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/model-servers.md#setup-preview).
- One task: `melo --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1 --chat-model MODEL --output-format json --timeout 300 -- "TASK"`; `--reasoning legacy|drop|replay|compress|compress+replay` (default `legacy`, unchanged) chooses whether a reply's reasoning is sent back, with `--reasoning-field auto|reasoning_content|reasoning` (replay and compress+replay), `--replay-turns N` and `--note-writer auto|heuristic` (compress modes: each reply becomes a RAM-only note and its drafts), `--retriever auto|off|bm25|llm|embedding`, `--recall-at start,attempt,step,tool`, `--recall-k 1..10`, `--recall-kinds note,draft,thought,digest,reflection,long`, `--recall-placement tool|message`, `--recall-min-score 0..1`, `--retrieval-extra-body JSON`, `--admit-on-outcome on|off` and `--keep-decision-text` (R6-lite's typed long store: a candidate is admitted by rehearsal, a user request (which also admits the fact after its marker) or statement, or the outcome switch; one decision per action; `--keep-decision-text` is refused in the UI), and `long_term.db` `user_version` 1 with the typed columns and `decisions` (legacy migrates in place, rows and search unchanged); `melo-retrieve --export-store DIR|FILE`, `--export-decisions DIR|FILE`, `--route CANDIDATES.jsonl --memory-dir DIR` (one action line per input; an optional `task_key` is stored in the digest's provenance, and `REFUSED` means a boundary or admission refusal) score the store offline (a directory with no store prints zero and exits 0); R5: compress recalls at start/attempt/step by default; auto = embedding if configured, else llm at start/attempt and bm25 at step/tool; tool is never on unless named; a step's recall can include a superseded note or thought chunk of an evicted turn, and `memory_stats.recall_empty` counts a recall that found nothing; legacy refuses these flags); `--workspace DIR` makes the run work in that folder: file tools stay inside it and `shell_exec`/`python_exec` start there (default: the current folder; a path that is not a folder exits 2 with one line); a direct run offers `file_read`, `file_write` and `python_exec`, and `--builtins all` adds `shell_exec` (off by default) and `list_files`, `--builtins shell_exec` only the shell; exit 0 completed, 1 crashed or a configuration error, 2 any other status or a usage error. Bare `melo` in a terminal opens the interactive UI (a first run asks for a model server and model and saves them, as `ollama` when the server answers `GET /api/version` like Ollama, else as `vllm`; thinking, tool calls and progress shown live, approvals (with a diff for an overwritten file), `/help` (the everyday commands; `/help all` every one), `/model`, `/backend`, `/verbose`, `/thinking`, `/stream`, `/expand`, `/progress`, `/approvals` (and Shift+Tab, Ask and Auto), `/grants [revoke N]` (what the person allowed, numbered), `/status` (five rows: model and whether it answers, folder, session, approvals in words, context use; `/status all` adds the tools, memory, limits and the cache, context, steps and tasks rows built from events already received, `--` where a server reports no `cached_tokens`), `/mcp`, `/retry`); `--mcp-config FILE` or the config's top-level `mcp_config` loads MCP servers; without a TTY it exits 2. `melo --serve` starts the gateway (`--port 0`: a free port, printed at startup). A first run marks models the server reports as loaded (oMLX `GET /v1/models/status`, Ollama `GET /api/ps`) and defaults to the first loaded chat model. With several chat models and none known loaded (a 401 or no status route, or none in memory) there is no default: the prompt asks for a number or id, a piped empty answer exits 2, and `melo --base-url URL` without `--chat-model` (the UI, a task, `--brief` or `melo ""`) first lists the server's models and uses the only chat model or the loaded one; several and none known loaded exits 2 listing the models (a 401 from the status route adds a line saying the server needs a key; pass `--chat-model <id>`; `--brief`: a `startup_error` result with `exit_code` 2); a list that cannot be read keeps `default`, with a stderr warning in text output. Agents: do not run bare `melo` in a pty under the user's HOME, and use direct mode in scripts.
- arm64 macOS development app, signed ad hoc: `uv run python scripts/build_macos_app.py --install` builds it into `~/Applications/LocalMelo.app` (replaced only when its bundle id is `org.localmelo.app`) and links `~/.local/bin/melo` only when no other `melo` is on `PATH`; `--uninstall` removes both and nothing else; the Swift compiler is `DEVELOPER_DIR`, else `/Applications/Xcode.app`, else the `xcode-select -p` folder when it holds `swiftc` (the Command Line Tools), else the build stops with `xcode-select --install`; see [macOS app](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/macos-app.md); the page instance check is not authentication, it checks the port owner and the instance before sending any login code, binds the code to that instance, attaches to a running gateway the endpoint file names (127.0.0.1, live pid, `GET /` id; same listener, instance and one-use-code checks; Quit leaves it running, menu `Quit localmelo (the gateway keeps running)`), else starts its gateway with `--port 0` and reads the port from the startup line `Gateway: http://127.0.0.1:PORT` (20 s start deadline); its window shows a native starting view (Melo's portrait, a poster of the moves: startup's last frame, sitting and smiling, while it starts and once ready, the error still (ears back, head low) on failure, via `startPortrait` in `PetPolicy.swift`) and, when the gateway cannot start or stops, an in-window failure with Try Again, Open Log and Quit (no dialog, the app stays open); it signs its web view in using one-use gateway login codes, offers "Sign in again" after a token rotation, and quit asks only when a chat or task would stop, something waits for an answer, or the health reply does not say (it quits at once otherwise), and its dialog names what would stop; the menu-bar item is the localmelo logo (`macos/assets/MenuBarLogo.png`, in colour, not a template image) with the running count beside it and a red dot while `status.waiting` (chats and tasks with an approval to answer) is not empty, its "Waiting for your approval" entry opens that chat or task, and the build copies the app icon, the committed `macos/assets/AppIcon.icns` (the whole emblem on a rounded tile of its own paper colour; `uv run --with pillow python scripts/make_app_icons.py` makes it from `docs/assets/melo.png`, and `scripts/art_pack.py apply` from a pack's `brand/` pictures); the build leaves tkinter, turtle, IDLE, pip, setuptools, ensurepip and 2to3 out of the bundled Python (`UNUSED` in the script, 36 MB), so `python_exec` under the app's `melo` cannot import them; the window, Dock and menus call the app localmelo, and `LocalMelo.app` is only the file name. Every picture of Melo in the app and the console comes from the moves; only the brand (app icon, menu-bar logo, the site's `docs/assets/melo.png` and `icon_small.png`) stays apart. Melo's moves (animated states `startup`, `thinking`, `working`, `attention`, `idle_rest`, `idle_play`) are one copy in `support/gateway/static/moves` (a 4 x 4 WebP sheet of 256 px frames per state, `poster-<state>.webp` per state, the stills `poster-done|error|offline.webp` (the pack's `stills/`), `face-idle|working|waiting|done|error|brand.png` 96 px heads (done and error from their stills, idle and brand from the smiling and calm heads drawn for small sizes), `favicon-16|32|64.png`, `manifest.json` with durations, `once`/`loop`, posters, poses, fades and the anchor; 1.6 MB), read by the app from its bundled package and made by `scripts/art_pack.py check|apply|figures PACK` (`--with pillow==13.0.0`, libwebp 1.6.0; a folder or a zip; `check` writes nothing, `apply` also replaces `support/cli/mark.py` and the brand pictures; engines `build_moves.py`, `make_app_icons.py`) from an art pack kept outside the repository, whose format and rules are in the [Art pack guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/art-pack.md); `static/moves.mjs` and `PetMoves.swift` play them by the same rules (cross-fade from the screen, `attention` interrupts, the latest request wins, the same state never restarts, `startup` once then holds, posters under reduced motion, a hidden player stops its clock); the panel's portrait (`portraitMove`) and the desktop pet (`petMove`, `PetMovePicker`) map waiting to `attention`, work to `working` or, when every running item is `answering`, `thinking`, rest to `idle_rest` with one `idle_play` after 20 s at most every 5 minutes, and the first move at rest to `startup`; done, error, offline (the page cannot reach the gateway) and unknown show a still: done (eyes closed and happy, tail up), error (ears back, head low), unknown and offline the offline still (curled up) at 60% opacity; the pet's stills (`petStill`, `PetStill`) are the same, a failed or stopped app, no model and an unreachable model server `error`, unknown `offline` at 0.6; moves that cannot be read are logged once, the pet then shows the offline still alone if it can; only Reduce Motion stills the pet's moves. After the wake-up both sit 8 s on its last frame, then rest; the console's portrait shows the resting poster after 3 min of plain rest and draws nothing scrolled out of view (the pet keeps moving). The app reads the moves inside its bundled package (`runtimeMovesFolder`), no second copy; a sheet that cannot be read shows its `poster-<state>.webp`. The faces (the reply icon: the newest reply shows its turn's state through `turnFace` in `turns.mjs`: `working`, `waiting` while an approval is open, `done`, `error`; every older reply and a stopped turn `idle`), the approval bar, the sidebar brand, the Main chat avatar, the tab icon and the activity pill's portrait are the moves' faces. The empty chat shows `moves/poster-startup.webp`. `macos/LocalMeloApp/PetPolicy.swift` is the pet's pure state policy (`petMood`: failure, `status.waiting`, work, `configured` false or `model_server.reachable` false (`noModel`, `unreachable`), `status.waiting`, work, `status.recent` done or failed 8 s each (the console's 8 s), rest, sleep after 60 s of quiet; `petMove`, `petStill`, `petThinking`, `PetMovePicker`). `macos/LocalMeloApp/PetPanel.swift` is the desktop pet: a borderless, non-activating `NSPanel` (132 x 97 pt, `.floating`, `canHide` false, no shadow, `.canJoinAllSpaces` + `.stationary` + `.ignoresCycle`, never key) that `petShouldShow` shows only while the main window is closed, minimized or the app is hidden (`petWindowShown`) and the person has not chosen Hide Melo; it sits at the bottom right of the first screen above the Dock, a press that moves more than 3 pt drags it (a drop within 12 pt of the bottom edge snaps) and its spot is saved per screen (display UUID, offset from the usable area's bottom-right corner), back on screen when the screens change; the file is `~/Library/Application Support/LocalMelo/pet.json` under `$HOME` (`hidden`, `pill`, `screen`, `spots`; a damaged file gives the defaults); a click opens the window, or the chat or task of the first `status.waiting` item while the mood is waiting; its menu is Open localmelo, Hide Melo, On the desktop, Quit localmelo, and **Show Melo** is in the menu-bar menu only while Melo is hidden; the health reply the app already polls feeds it (`PetController.update`), it has no timer of its own and works its mood out on each reply, touch (hover, click, drag) and window change; VoiceOver reads one button with `PetMood.label` and `help`, and the pet posts no announcement of its own when a wait starts (the menu-bar item announces it, so VoiceOver does not read it twice). `macos/LocalMeloApp/PillPolicy.swift` is the activity pill's pure policy and `PillPanel.swift` its panel. While the window is put away (`petWindowShown`) and the choice is Melo and the pill (`PetSettings.mode`: `hidden` is Nothing, else `pill` true is the default Melo and the pill and false Melo only; Show Melo restores the earlier `pill`), `PillPolicy.update` turns each health reply into a `PillDecision` (`pill` or nil, `petShowsDone`, `recheckIn`): `status.waiting` first (`Waiting for your approval`, amber, a press opens the first waiting chat or task), else with work running and `model_server.reachable` false `Model server not reachable`, else `status.focus.activity` and `icon` (`Working` when `focus` is null; `+N` is `status.running` summed minus one), else `status.recent` done (`Done: <title>`) or failed (`Stopped: <title>`), 8 s each as the pet's moods (a stopped run shows nothing), counted from `ended_s_ago` plus the reply's age; a reply older than 12 s is not believed; a changed line of the same state waits until 1.5 s after the last change (a new state shows at once); `PillPolicy.dismiss` (the `×`) hides it until something not running then runs, or anything runs once all has stopped, and a dismissed run's end stays hidden; while the pill is hidden the pet is shown, and after a `Done` that ran out the pet shows its done still for 3 s. The panel is a 48 pt capsule in a 5 pt clear margin (a HUD blur under a tint, a 36 pt portrait whose ring is the state's colour, from the moves' `face-working|waiting|done|error.png`, the line at 14 pt cut with an ellipsis at 320 pt); it sits at the pet's saved spot with its right edge at the pet's, clamped to the screen's usable area (`pillPlacement`, `pillResized`, `pillDropped`; a drop saves the pet's `PetSpot`); a press opens the focus item's route (`consoleRoute`; `status.recent`'s for an end) or the window, hover shows `×`, and right-click is the pet's menu, whose submenu `On the desktop` (also in the menu-bar menu, one `DesktopMenu` check mark) chooses `Melo and the activity pill`, `Melo only` or `Nothing`; VoiceOver reads one button (`Melo is reading example.com. Opens the chat.`) with the action `Hide until the next task`; it breathes (scale 1.04 in 3.2 s) only while working and pulses its ring three times when a wait begins, both only while `shouldAnimate` holds, and its only timer is the one `recheckIn` asks for. The mood still comes from the 2 s health poll (the gateway has no all-sessions event stream: its streams are per session, so telling the pet sooner would need a new endpoint and an event client in the app). `/api/health` `status.recent` is `null` or `{kind, id, title, outcome, ended_s_ago}` (`title` at most 200 characters, empty when unreadable) of the newest finished chat turn, task, run or terminal turn (`outcome` `done|failed|stopped`). `/api/health` `sessions.store_reason` distinguishes `owned`, `open-error`, `failed` and healthy `null`.
- Provider `stream_chat` yields provisional raw fragments and a completed reply; close on early exit, never persist raw deltas. `StreamFilter` buffers without a framing declaration; a trusted `reasoning_tags` hint allows line-level redacted release (an open PEM private key block is held until its END line, or past 16 KiB its body is dropped as it arrives). Only the interactive UI consumes it, and it does by default (`[cli] stream = true` is the default; `-X cli.stream=false` for one run, `melo config set cli.stream false` for good) with per-model `[cli.reasoning_tags]` (`explicit`, `closing_only`, `none`) and `/stream on|off` (`/new` and `/clear` reset it to `[cli] stream`; `[cli] status_line = "auto"|"off"` (default auto, no flag) adds the usage and work zones to the bottom bar; `off` keeps the run zone and `ctx` of the last request); a server that ignores `stream` (one JSON body) or ends the stream before any delta is read as a whole reply (`OpenAICompatLLM` asks once more without `stream` in the second case, marks the reply `StreamFragment.whole`, and does not ask that server to stream again; the UI prints `This server sends replies whole; melo shows them when they are complete.` once), while a stream that breaks after a delta keeps `Streaming response ended before completion`; released text shows in the live area, provisional text prints once to scrollback labelled, the final answer prints once, and only that UI streams; an invalid `[cli]` value warns instead of failing a run. [provider reference](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/reference/python-api.md#custom-model-providers).
- A reply that starts (after whitespace, any letter case) with a closed `<thinking>...</thinking>` block has that block as its thinking, as a `<think>` block does (`split_thinking`, the stream filter with no hint or the hint `explicit`, `has_think_block`); a `<thinking>` later in the text, or never closed, stays text, and `[cli.reasoning_tags]` `none` keeps the tags literal. A planning reply whose text has no letter or digit in any script (`...`, dashes, emoji) is an empty reply: the model is asked once more (`has_content` in `localmelo.melo.schema`).
- Unfinished thinking: a planning reply with no tool call is unfinished when its content opens `<think>` and never closes it (unless the model's `[cli.reasoning_tags]` is `none`), it has no answer once thinking is set aside and the provider counted `reasoning_tokens`, a streamed reply's content repeats its reasoning word for word, or it has no thinking and no `</think>` while the model's framing ends thinking with a mark (`closing_only` declared by the interactive UI, or `field`: an earlier reply of this provider had reasoning in its own field and this one's usage reports `reasoning_tokens` 0). Its `assistant.message` has all the text as `thinking` and `content` `""`; it counts as an empty reply with a `notice` of kind `unfinished_answer` (`detail` `{}`) and one more planning request; a row of 2 replies without an answer that held one ends `failed` with the error `melo did not finish an answer` (constant `UNFINISHED_ANSWER_ERROR` in `localmelo.melo.schema`), `result` `""`. The text is never `result`, `last_text` or a best effort. Terminal: dim notice, the reply as thinking (`✻ Thought`), end line `melo did not finish an answer.` + `/retry, or try another model.`; console: folded thinking, failure card title `melo did not finish an answer`, filled **Try again**. With thinking off (the provider's request carries `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking` false, or `think` false for Ollama; `BaseLLMProvider.thinking_off`) the last two rules do not apply, and a reply with no tool call and no answer text whose reasoning field holds words, with no `reasoning_tokens` counted, takes those words as its `content` (`thinking` `""`), whole or streamed (`melo.schema.answer_from_thinking`, applied in `Chat._send`); counted reasoning tokens, or a `<think>` never closed, still make a reply unfinished.
- Empty turn after thinking (#469; developer setting, default on): `[agent] empty_reply_fallback = "on"|"off"` (`-X agent.empty_reply_fallback=off`; saved only when `off`; direct runs and sessions read it). On: when a row's second reply has no tool call and no words but the provider reported reasoning, the agent asks once more with thinking off (only where the service has a switch), and if still empty the answer is the last lines of the thinking, ending with `(from melo's thinking)`, and the run completes. Off: the run ends `failed` with `melo did not finish an answer`, as before. `RunResult.empty_reply` (also in `--json` and `run.finished`) is `{"thinking_off_retry": bool, "from_thinking": bool}`, absent when neither; the `notice` events are `thinking_off_retry` and `answer_from_thinking` (`detail` `{}`).
- Tool call written as text (`broken_tool_call` in `localmelo.melo.schema`): a planning reply with no tool call is no answer when its text (reasoning split off, outside code fences and backticks) holds a tag `<function_calls>`, `<tool_call>`, `<arg_key>`, `<invoke name=`, `<function invoke`, `<function=` or `<parameter=` (any case) at the start of the text or of a line, or followed by `{`, `<`, a line break or the end (never in the middle of a sentence), or a token `<|python_tag|>`, `[TOOL_CALLS]`, `<|tool_call|>`, `<function_call>`, `<｜tool▁calls▁begin｜>` or `<|tool_calls_section_begin|>` at the start of the text or of a line, or `to=functions.` followed by a name anywhere; or, judged against the tools offered on the step (names of 3+ characters), is as a whole a JSON call object or a list of them (or one fenced `json` or `tool_code` block), or has a line that is wholly one (an offered tool as `name` and an `arguments` or `parameters` key; JSON of only parameter names, or of a `name` and a description, is data, not a call), starts with an offered tool's name, `(` and an argument (`name=`, a quote, `{`, `[`) or `)` (`file_read(path) reads a file` is a sentence), or starts with a parameter name (case-sensitive) followed by nothing, `=`, `<`, a line break, a colon with no space after it, or an emoji (`text`, `text=…`, `text:abc`, `text` + line break + words, `text✅ 已记录`; not `text is short`, `Text messages…`, `text-based`, `text：好的`, `text→speech`, `level>3`, `text ✅`); or holds a call id that leaked into the text (`call_00_` and 16+ letters or digits, or `call_` and 20+) and is under 80 characters or starts with a parameter name (`text call_00_CfS77joytXzYfQlV455l3697`; a long answer that mentions an id, or `call_abc`, is an answer; this rule needs no tools). A one-word reply equal to a parameter name (`path`) is flagged too: the cost of catching the bare `text` a server leaves behind. A flagged reply counts as an empty reply with the label `[tool call written as text]`, its own nudge and a `notice` of kind `tool_call_as_text` (`detail` `{"count"}`; sent for the reply that ends the run too, before `run.finished`, so a display drops its text, with the message `The model wrote a tool call as text, so it did not run.`, and in a step after its `note` event and before its `recall` event), is never `last_text`, and a row of 2 empty or broken replies that held one ends `failed` with the error `tool call written as text` (`TOOL_CALL_TEXT_ERROR`; a row that also held unfinished thinking keeps `melo did not finish an answer`), `result` `""`. `answer_on_stop` and the explanation of an Auto block (no tools are offered there) drop a reply with such markup; the task views (park card, last note, `task follow`) do not know the offered tools, so they skip markup-shaped replies only (`text✅ 已记录` still shows there). The `assistant.message` still holds what the model sent; the terminal and the console show the dim notice, not the text, live and replayed. The console's `splitThinking` (`static/turns.mjs`) reads a leading closed `<thinking>` block like `split_thinking`; `tests/fixtures/display_vectors.json` holds the shared cases.
- No-answer label: with `record_answers`, a run with no answer leaves `INTERRUPT_LABEL` (`cancelled`) or `NO_ANSWER_LABEL` (any other status) in the window and in the saved turn, which people read; a request carries `UNANSWERED_NOTE` as a user message in its place (`Chat._send`), joined to the user messages beside it, because a model copies an assistant message that says it gave no answer.
- Fixed prefix is the default: `[agent] fixed_prefix = false` or `--fixed-prefix off` sends the earlier requests, `--fixed-prefix on|off` overrides the config. Local date and UTC offset freeze per run; legacy long-term recall is read at a run's first step and kept (read again only after the window drops its oldest messages, and at the next run), so each planning request extends the previous one; `fixed-prefix-v2` puts the latest reflection last under `cache_layout v2` and makes a reflection request repeat the latest plan request (same tools) plus one final user message; `all` freezes sorted schemas while `retrieve` remains dynamic. `prefix_cache.schema_changes` counts changes, not measured server misses; cached tokens appear only when reported for planning/reflection.
- Window eviction: `[agent] window_eviction = "chunk"|"boundary"|"slide"` or `--window-eviction`. `chunk` (default) drops down to 12 messages, and the prompt-cap fit and the `--context-window` fit down to 70% of their limit, keeping the cut until a request passes the limit; `boundary` also drops a finished attempt at the next attempt; `slide` drops one unit per step once the 20-message window is full. Modes other than `slide` add `config.window_eviction` to the JSON result.
- Cache layout (default `v3`): `[agent] cache_layout = "v2"|"v3"` or `--cache-layout`. `v3` with the fixed prefix appends a reflection once at the attempt boundary as a window message, keeps the reflection request and reply in the window, and retries an unreadable reflection on the same prefix; `v2` (the earlier requests) rebuilds the reflection as the last message of every plan request; no effect without the fixed prefix. `--window-messages N` / `[agent] window_messages` (8-256) is the window's message cap: default 64 on a local server and for `--base-url`, 20 on a cloud vendor; a value you set wins; under `chunk`/`boundary` the prompt-size fit evicts in chunks. `--cache-layout v2 --window-messages 20` send the earlier requests. `config.cache_layout` is in the JSON result unless `v2`, `config.window_messages` unless 20.
- `--reflect-tool-guard on|off` (default `on`; `[agent] reflect_tool_guard = false` also turns it off): on makes every reflection request offer the tools of that step's planning request and end with `Answer with the JSON object only; do not call any tool.`; `tool_choice` and the retry are unchanged. The `reflection` event's `unreadable_reason` is `tool_call`, `invalid`, `no_json` or `null`.
- Reflection reading (`reflection_gate` `patient` or `flags`; no option): a reply with no reflection as it stands gets one repair of a `{...}` the decoder rejects (the first 8 per reply): drop the `]` or `}` at the error that no opener matches (`unmatched_closer`), a comma before a closer (`trailing_comma`), escape raw newline, carriage return and tab characters in strings (`control_char`), double the backslash of an `Invalid \escape` (`invalid_escape`), or insert a `]` before the comma that precedes the key at which the decoder stopped inside an array (`unclosed_array`); it counts only with a valid `recommended_action`, two repairs (a second invalid escape included) or text that stops short stay unreadable. The `reflection` event's `repaired` names it, else `null`. A retry after `invalid` or `no_json` with rejected JSON adds the line `Your reply was not valid JSON (<error> at character <n>: ...<up to 60 characters>...). Reply again with one JSON object.` after the retry note; `tool_call` and `--reflection-gate utility` are unchanged.
- The cache settings are the defaults of direct runs, the interactive UI, the gateway and `AgentOptions()`; `--fixed-prefix off --window-eviction slide --reflect-tool-guard off` (hidden from default help, listed by `melo --developer --help`) send the earlier requests byte for byte. A config key you set stays, a missing key is the default, saving writes a key only when it differs. The JSON result gains `prefix_cache` and `config.window_eviction`, `config.reflect_tool_guard` by default.
- Cache telemetry: the `usage` of `assistant.message` and `reflection` events also has `cached_tokens` and `reasoning_tokens` when the server sent them (streamed with `stream_options.include_usage` too; absent means not reported, never 0; summed over a reflection's requests), and `prefix` (`null` for a run's first request, else `{messages, chars, against: {kind, request}, previous_messages, total_messages, first_changed, tools_changed, fresh_chars, request_chars}`: how much of the best earlier plan or reflect request of the run this one repeats, and the role of the first message that changed; on `reflection` it is for its first request). Request bodies and the JSON result are unchanged. `python scripts/cache_report.py LOG` prints one row per request (kind plan or reflect) from a `stream-json` log, then totals by kind and overall and a `reusable` line (`cached / (prompt - fresh)`, `fresh` estimated from `prefix.fresh_chars` / `prefix.request_chars`, which also hold the characters no earlier request of the run had). See docs/reference/events.md.
- Confined writes (macOS, `[agent] confine_writes`, default true; `-X agent.confine_writes=false` turns it off): `--brief`/`melo worker` runs and gateway saved tasks start `shell_exec` and `python_exec` (checks included) under `sandbox-exec`: file writes only in the workspace (`--workspace`, else cwd), `.melo-tmp` there (`TMPDIR`/`TMP`/`TEMP`; self-gitignored; kept with the workspace), the user's own temp folder (`confstr(_CS_DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR)`, `/var/folders/.../T`: macOS `mktemp`/`mktemp -d` write there whatever `TMPDIR` says; `/tmp` stays refused), uv's cache (`UV_CACHE_DIR`, `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/uv` or `~/.cache/uv`), `~/Library/Caches/black` (`BLACK_CACHE_DIR`), `~/.npm` (`npm_config_cache`), `/dev/null|zero|tty|stdout|stderr|dtracehelper|ptmx`, `/dev/fd/*`, `/dev/ttys*`, and for a linked git worktree its own git dir plus the common `objects` (status/diff/add work; commit to a branch, refs, config and the main checkout are refused). Reads and the network are not confined. A tool text with `Operation not permitted` gets a first line (after `[exit code N]`) `melo: writing outside the workspace is not allowed in this run (refused: PATH); write in ROOT, and put scratch files in $TMPDIR.`; `run.confinement` = `{"writes": "confined", "refused_writes": N}` (off macOS `{"writes": "not_confined", "reason": ...}`; absent when off). Cannot apply (no `sandbox-exec`, nested sandbox refused) = `startup_error` before any command: `writes cannot be confined to the workspace: WHY; set agent.confine_writes to false to run without it (-X agent.confine_writes=false for one run)`. Chats (terminal UI, console, app), the gateway's chat sessions and, by default, plain direct runs: unchanged, unconfined. Developer setting `[agent] confine_direct_runs` (default false, no flag; `-X agent.confine_direct_runs=true` for one run; `melo config keys confine` lists it): true confines plain direct runs too, i.e. `melo "TASK"` (with or without `--workspace`; else cwd is the workspace) and the `melo ""` loop, exactly as above, and `run.confinement` is in the JSON result; `--brief` runs and saved tasks keep `confine_writes`. Cannot apply = stderr `melo: error: writes cannot be confined to the workspace: WHY; set agent.confine_direct_runs to false to run without it (-X agent.confine_direct_runs=false for one run)` and exit 1 (no JSON on stdout). Off, a direct run is byte for byte as before. Python: `AgentOptions(confine_writes=True)`.
- `--brief-items on|off` (experimental, default off; `[agent] brief_items = true`): with `--brief`, reflection requests and the check two steps before the last attempt ends list the brief's numbered items no edit has touched yet (marks from `git status`; edits only, never "done"); each use emits a `brief_items` notice.
- Captured history is opt-in via `[agent] captured_history = true` or `--captured-history on`; `off` overrides config. The separate history copy is pattern-redacted and capped at 200,000 characters per result; acquisition omissions are unknown. Model previews use a 50,000-character limit. Redaction can miss secrets.
- Memory across chats (`[memory] across_chats`, default `true`; console and app chats only): notes are kept two ways, never confirmed. (1) A typed remember request (signal lexicon `request_facts` plus `keep in mind (that)`, `make a note (that)`, `帮我记一下`; EN/ZH) is kept by code before the run, under `people` only when its fact is about a person (`Marco's studio …`, `Marco lives in …`, `马可住在…`), else `about`. (2) The chat model calls tool `remember(text, topic)` (`topic` one of the five; tier `read`, no approval) when the user shares something lasting or a finished task's result is worth keeping; `NOTES_TEXT` and the tool's description tell it to keep a plain statement of a lasting fact about the user (where they live, their name, a person, their schedule, a preference; “I live in Utrecht.”, “我的导师是周教授。”) with `remember` in that turn, a change too (“I changed jobs; I work at Acme now.” → `You work at Acme.`, which replaces the old note); a note is one sentence written to the user in the second person, so “you” in it is the user, in the language of the user's message in this turn (`NOTES_TEXT`, the tool texts and the block header say so; `NOTES_TEXT` says recalled items answer the question whether or not they were kept as notes (an earlier message of this chat or another counts as much as a note); neither it nor the tool text says when a save may be claimed (quoting the tool's outputs was imitated, and a claim rule made the model refuse recalled facts; `ChatMemory.keep_claims` makes a claimed save real instead); `NOTES_TEXT` also says reminders are scheduled, not noted: a request to be reminded at a time is never saved as a note; every header starts with `[melo's memory ·`, and `localmelo.melo.memory.block.strip_block` cuts a message there), and the chat answers with the newest value only and uses only the notes that answer the question. Developer setting `[memory] keep_statements` (default `false`; `-X memory.keep_statements=on`; `melo -h all` lists it; for comparison only): after a completed run, code keeps the clear cases the model left (`ChatMemory.keep_statements`, `records.statements`): a plain first-person sentence of the typed text naming a subject (`I live in`, `my X is`, `call me`, `我的X是`, `我在X工作`, …) with a lasting value; never a question, to-do, hypothetical, negation, past, someone's opinion, passing state (`my build is failing`), remember request or secret, nor one a note of the turn covers (same subject or overlap >= 0.6); `admitted_by` `user_statement`, published like a `remember` note. A chat's own turns the model's window no longer holds are recalled like another chat's and read `this chat, <day>` (`recall.in_view`/`this_chat`; `SessionRunner._recall` passes the window to `before_turn`, `window_start` finds the oldest turn whose user message it holds from the time stamp of its first user message, and without a window the whole chat is left out as before; `search_memory` leaves out the turns still in the window). `NOTES_TEXT` begins `You remember the recent messages of this conversation, not all of it.` and says older parts of it, earlier chats and notes come back when they match. `remember` refuses: memory off or no chat turn (`CHAT_TURN` contextvar set by `before_turn`), an empty note, `sensitive()` (sets `refused`), a note that says both a first-person word (`I`, `I'm`, `I've`, `I'll`, `I'd` with a capital `I`, `me`, `my`, `mine`, `myself`, `我` not followed by `们`; never we/our/us; quoted spans and a numeral such as `Phase I` are skipped) and `you`/`your`/`yours`/`你`/`您`, or a first-person word with the user in the third person (`records.names_user`: `the user`, `user`, `the person`, `用户`; its `I` is melo, never rewritten) (`WRITE_IN_YOU`: `Not remembered: write the user as "you" and the assistant as "melo", never "I" or "my" (not "I prefer that when you explain …" but "You prefer that melo explains …").`), and a note whose content words (stopwords, restating and function words such as user/prefer/call/name/said/then/each/use/melo/who/whom/whose/which/where/when aside; ASCII stemmed twice, `-ies` and long `-ie` end in `y`, a doubled consonant an `-ing`/`-ed` brought drops one (`running` and `run`; `l`, `s`, `z`, `f`, `d` stay); CJK chars and bigrams, a bigram also matching with one char between; every value, meaning a word with a digit, a number word, a weekday, capitalised word inside a sentence, quoted span or CJK char, must be found, and at least 80% of the other words) do not all match the user's typed text of this chat's turns (current + earlier, not undone) or, then admitted as `outcome` with empty quote, in the index documents of `task`/`front_bg` sessions this chat recalled (`turn.memory` `used`); the refusal starts `Not remembered: not something the user said.` and names up to 3 missing words (values first), plus `Write it in the language the user used.` when a missing word's script is not the typed text's. A note with a first-person word and no `you` is first rewritten with `records.second_person(note, protect=True)` (so `My flight to Porto is at gate 22.` is kept as `Your flight to Porto is at gate 22.`, and the reply `Remembered: …` shows it), before the evidence and owner checks. For `user_statement`, `records.wrong_owner(note, quote)` reads whose each sentence is by its first words (`my|our|your|the user's|我的|你的|您的` = the user; `Name's …`, `马可的…` = a third party, only when the name is a person's (`people.person`, or a reduplicated nickname such as `思思`); a contraction such as `That's`, a time word, a language or tool (`Python's GIL`) or a modifier before `的` (`开发的代码…`) reads none) and refuses a third-party typed sentence with a user note (`Not remembered: that is about NAME, not the user. Write the note about them: “NAME's …”.`) or the reverse (`Not remembered: the user said that about themselves, not about NAME. Write the note to the user: “Your …”.`) unless the name is in the other sentence. `quote_for` and the statement and request readers split sentences with `records._split`: a title (`Mr|Mrs|Ms|Mx|Dr|Prof|St|Jr|Sr|Mt`), `vs.`, `etc.` before a lowercase word or digit, `No.` before a digit and a capital initial other than `I` before a capitalised word end none. Kept: `Remembered: TEXT …`; a repeat: `Already remembered: TEXT`; a same-subject note supersedes; `admitted_by` `user_statement` (quote = the best typed sentence) or `outcome`. Each note is a second-person sentence in `~/.cache/localmelo/memory/records.db` (`SqliteLongTerm(records=True)`, `user_version` 2, columns `topic`, `quote`, `edited_at`; topics `about`, `preferences`, `people`, `projects`, `decisions`); text that looks like a key, password, code, card or ID number is refused; a same-subject note supersedes (any topic, requests and `remember` alike: `records.subject` keys from I/you/user live in|work at|go by|is named, call me, my|your|the user's X is, (I|you|we|the user) have|has|had (a|an|my|your)? X on|at|in|every Y (relation `on`, same subject as "X is on Y"; CJK not covered), (我|你|用户)(的)X是|叫|姓, 住在, 在X工作 (`home` also from `I|we (have) moved to`/`(我|你|用户)搬到|搬去`; a verb key's value is `unit` when it has a digit or 楼/层/室/号/栋/单元/floor/apt/apartment/room/unit/suite/building, else place/name, and values of different kinds are different subjects: Utrecht vs 3楼 never replace each other), with the value related the same way (is on/at/in/called, a description such as `a`/`very`/`是…的`, or a plain value); a third party's `Name's X is …` (`Dr.`/`Prof.`/`Mrs.`, multi-word names) or `NAME的X是|叫|姓|在 …` is a subject keyed by its owner (`tom briggs's office`), so "Tom Briggs's office is in room 9C." never replaces "Your manager is Tom Briggs."; two different subjects never; else with vectors cosine >= 0.8 and one changed value span <= 8 tokens; else same kind and overlap >= 0.6, but not when a note's subject (not a verb key) has a word the other's text lacks; the old note stays `superseded`, never recalled, listed or pinned, and `?undo=true` on the new one restores it; a turn whose note was replaced (`provenance.replaces`) is recalled after the newer note, which is added if missing, with ` (older; replaced by a newer note)` on its line and ` · older; replaced by a newer note` on its `source`; without a note, of two chat turns whose typed plain statements give one subject different values (or, with vectors, two subjectless statements whose turns have cosine >= 0.8 and one changed value span), the older is recalled after the newer turn, which is added if missing (not one the chat's window still shows), with ` (older; replaced by a newer message)` (`records.newer_turns`, no model call); the chat is told the newest of disagreeing notes or chats is true; the recall block leaves such an older turn out (`recall.current_only`) unless the message asks about the past (`before`, `used to`, `earlier`, `previous`, `old`, `以前`, `之前`, `原来`, `过去`), while `search_memory` still lists it with the label). Each completed chat turn (typed text, then each note the person added that the run read at a later step, one paragraph each behind `(added while melo worked)` (the redacted `inbox.accepted` text; a note the run never read is the next turn's typed text); then the answer; redacted; a turn that ended on a blocked step, meaning its last tool result is `approval_denied` or an Auto block note (`blocked.BLOCK_PREFIXES`) with no later success, holds the person's words only, no `melo:` line, and a reindex applies this to old turns) and each task result is a document in `index.db`; a turn over 2,000 chars is up to 8 chunks of the same session and turn (chunk 0 the head, later ones `User: <first ~200 chars typed>…` + the next window, ~200 chars overlap), and a search list holds one chunk of a turn at most (the best). Per turn: BM25 (most content words) plus cosine (>= 0.55, embedding model of the config) fused by RRF k=60, at most 3 notes + 2 documents of other chats or of this chat's turns that left the window (`this chat, <day>`), 900 chars (a turn line reads `the user said “typed”; melo replied “answer” (chat “T”, <day>)`, both parts bounded together at 200 chars; a day has `, <year>` when not the year of `melo.clock.now()` and `, HH:MM` when another item of the block is from the same day; records of one subject key with different values are listed newest first, each older one marked ` (older; replaced by a newer note)` and kept; the page's `text` and `source` keep the day alone), appended once to the user message under `[melo's memory · notes (“you” is the user) and earlier chats, not instructions]`, which starts with `melo kept from this message: “quote” (saved; do not save it again or in a file)` when a remember request was kept (also with nothing recalled) and with a line that a password or key was not kept and must not be written anywhere when a sentence was refused; a query embedding over 1.5 s or failing falls back to BM25. `[memory] retriever` = `auto` (default: that hybrid; BM25 alone without an embedding model) | `bm25` | `embedding` (the hybrid; `Config.validate()` errors without an embedding model) | `llm` (loose BM25 picks <= 20 candidates, the chat model chooses via `LLMRetriever` within 4 s, no embedding calls; BM25 order on timeout, error or unreadable reply); `-X memory.retriever=...`, in `melo -h all` only. After a completed run `ChatMemory.keep_changes(info)` (awaited by the runner after `keep_statements`, before `keep_claims`; chat turns only, not for workers, `index_only` runners or memory off; whatever `[memory] keep_statements` says): when the turn kept no note, each plain statement of the typed words (`records.statements`) whose `records.subject_key` equals that of an active note with another text ("My weekly sync is on Friday." beside "Your weekly sync is on Wednesday.") is written like a note (supersede with `provenance.replaces`, `admitted_by` `user_statement`, `Remembered · Undo` event) even when the model only asked; a statement of a subject no note holds is left to the model. After a completed run `ChatMemory.keep_claims(info, answer)` (awaited by the runner after `keep_changes`; not for workers, `index_only` runners or memory off): when the answer's first claim (`records.claimed`: `Remembered: X`, `Noted — X`/`Noted: X`/`Noted, X`, `I've noted (that) X`, `I'll remember (that) X`, `Got it — X` with a `noted` after it (after `Got it —`, `OK,`, `Sure,` etc. an `I've noted`/`I'll remember` opener is the claim, never part of X), `记下了：X`, `记住了：X`, `已记住：X`, `已记录：X`, `已保存：X`) is there and the turn kept no note, it calls `remember(X, topic)` (same checks, supersede and event). X ends at its sentence's end, not at the `.` of a title (`Prof.`, `Mrs.`, `Dr.`). X must read as a statement: written to the user (you/your/yours, word-bounded, any case, or 你/您) or with a verb, copula or `'s` (`records._STATEMENT`: is/are/was/were/has/have/had/lives/works/starts/leaves/meets/teaches/coaches, `'s`, 是/在/叫/有/住), so a fact about another person (`Prof. Duarte's office is in the Atrium Wing.`) goes to `remember`, whose checks decide; otherwise X with 3 content words or more (`Gate 9 for Faro.`) is flagged and not saved. With no fact, a claim that is a sentence of its own is flagged too (`records._BARE`: `Saved.`, `Saved to memory`, `Noted.`, `Got it, noted…`, `Noted, thanks!`, `I've saved|stored|recorded|noted it|that|this`, `I'll remember it|that|this`, `已记录`, `记录了`, `已保存`, `保存了`, `已记住`, `记住了`, `记下了`, `已记下`, `帮你记下了`, with or without a leading ✅), also when it names only a pronoun or generic noun (`I've saved your preference.`, `我已经记录了你的偏好。`; a fact that is only such a noun, `Your preferences.`, is flagged too), while `Got it!`, `Thanks!`, `The file was saved.` and `I saved the file to disk.` are no claim. A refusal or an X that states nothing keeps nothing and sets `unsaved_claim` true. Event `turn.memory` (`used` (`[{kind, id, text, source, session_id, turn, at, shown}]`: `text` is the stored text, `shown` the exact line the model read in the recall block, as the recall settings made it, without a list number; an item left out of the block for room has no entry), `searched` (optional: what `search_memory` found this turn, same item shape as `used`, `shown` the line of the search result without its number, no repeats), `opened` (optional: `[{session_id, turn, id}]`, the chat turns `open_memory` opened this turn, one entry per turn; the opened text is in the tool result, not in the event), `remembered`, `refused`, `recall` = `{retriever, fallback: none|timeout|error|unreadable|no-embedding, embed_ms, search_ms, select_ms, select_tokens: {prompt, completion}, candidates, used, block_chars, query_from}` (`block_chars` = length of the block appended to the message, 0 when none; `query_from` = `message` | `recent` | `none`, what the search was for: `recent` = a message with no content of its own searched with the user's words of the chat's last turns, `none` = no search ran; absent from turns stored before it existed), `unsaved_claim` (bool, false unless the answer claimed a save and no note was kept), emitted on every turn with memory on, and again, whole, each time `remember` keeps a note or refuses a secret, `keep_changes` replaces a note or `keep_claims` flags the turn (a note that replaced this turn's request note drops it); the stored turn `result` has the same as `memory_recall`); tools `search_memory(query, scope=all|records|chats, k<=8)` and `remember(text, topic)`; `GET /api/memory/records`, `DELETE /api/memory/records/{id}[?undo=true]`; deleting a chat deletes its documents. Direct runs, workers, the terminal chat and the benchmark are unchanged (no `remember`). **Managing it (the Memory tab, `/memory`, `melo memory`):** `ChatMemory.edit_record(id, text)` rewords a note in place (`SqliteLongTerm.edit_entry`: `text`, vector, `provenance.quote` = the new text, `provenance.edited`, `edited_at`; an `EDIT` decision row; old text overwritten, decision text/sha blanked, WAL checkpointed; empty, over 300 chars or `sensitive()` raises `ValueError`); `delete_entry(id)` (no restore) also deletes the superseded older wordings it replaced and checkpoints the WAL; `forget_all()` empties `records.db` and `index.db` and stamps `meta.forgotten_at` in `index.db` so `reindex(store)` skips turns that ended before it; `forget_chat_notes(session_id)`; `reindex(store)` clears and rebuilds `index.db` from the session store (completed, not undone, answered turns; 16 per embedding batch) and re-embeds notes whose `embed_model` differs from the model now set. A note outlives its chat: `ConsoleSessions.delete(id, forget_notes=False)` / `DELETE /api/sessions/{id}?notes=forget`. API: `GET /api/memory/records[?session_id=]` (rows add `from`, `chat_gone`, `edited`; top level `documents`, `embedding_model`, `last_error`), `PATCH /api/memory/records/{id}` `{text}` (400 with the reason, 404), `DELETE /api/memory/records?all=true` (`{notes, turns}`; 400 without the flag), `PUT /api/memory` `{on}` (saves `[memory] across_chats`), `POST /api/memory/reindex`; `GET /api/models` adds `embedding_models` and `suggested_embedding`, `GET/PUT /api/settings` carry `across_chats`. `melo memory list [-n N] | forget [ID] [-y] | status | reindex` (`support/memory_cli.py`; `forget` asks with `onboard._ask_choice`: a list on a TTY with keep first, a typed number when piped, Esc/EOF keep; `reindex` exits 1 while the gateway owns `gateway/sessions.db`); terminal `/memory` is a `NotePicker` then `Back|Edit it|Delete it` (`support/cli/memory_notes.py`), `/memory window` is the old working-window view. The first-run and `melo setup` embedding question is `Remember across chats with MODEL?` (`Yes, with it`, `No, by words only`). Task starts and side chats (`ChatMemory`; the console's asks call `index_exchange`, and the main chat's `side.summary` listener `side_ended(event)` calls `side_summary` in the background for a finished task's ending, `data.source` not `chat`: a chat's own run is indexed as its turn already): `context_pack(objective, chat_id, budget_chars=1500, *, workspace=None) -> str` returns `""` (memory off or nothing qualifies) or `PACK_HEADER` plus lines in the recall block's rendering: About you, Preferences (and `feedback` when `records.TOPICS` has it, and notes with `provenance.source == "import"` other than People, Decisions, Projects) newest first; Projects notes whose `provenance.workspace` equals `workspace` by `os.path.realpath` (an import sets it, and so does a Projects note kept in a chat that has a folder, as that folder's `os.path.realpath`; no other topic stores one, a chat with no folder stores none); then `search(objective)` records of those topics (a Projects note of another known workspace is dropped); never People or Decisions; lowest-ranked lines dropped whole at `budget_chars`; no chat-model call, the 1.5 s query embedding falls back to words. `side_summary(side_session_id, title, summary, *, workspace=None)` indexes one document of kind `side_summary` (turn `-1`, text `Summary of chat “<title>”: <summary>`, redacted, at most 2,000 characters; a second call replaces it; `forget_session` deletes it; `reindex` keeps it; label `chat “<title>” · summary`; never recalled to its own chat). `index_exchange(task_session_id, request, answer)` indexes kind `agent_exchange` (turns `-2`, `-3`, …; `Task asked: … Answer: …`). Neither is a note. A turn the person did not begin (`TurnInfo.origin` not empty, such as a task's question `ask_owner`; `is_owner_question`) is recalled for by its `user_text` but writes no notes: `remember` returns `Not remembered: this turn is a task's question, not the user's words.`, `keep_statements`, `keep_claims` and `keep_changes` return `[]`, it is no evidence for `remember` in later turns, and `after_turn` and `reindex` skip it.
- Sleep (`support/memory/sleep.py`; developer setting `[memory] sleep` = `off` (default) | `rules` | `model` | `model+tags`, validated by `config.MEMORY_SLEEP`, saved only when not `off`, `-X memory.sleep=rules`, listed in `option_tiers.EXPERIMENTAL_KEYS` as `#363`): `ChatMemory.sleep(variant=None, *, now=None, chats=None, budget=None, began=None) -> SleepReport` and `undo_sleep(run_id)`. `rules` makes no chat-model call; an existing-fact check may embed a candidate (1.5 s, cached per text, cosine >=0.85 (`HELD_COSINE`) on comparable vectors; word fallback otherwise). at most `MAX_CHANGES` = 20 changes per run, each `Change{op, before_ids, after_id, text, source_turn, quote, before_texts, verdict, proposal, guard}` (`quote` is evidence, rule fallback <=300 characters; `before_texts` aligns with `before_ids`; no export/training yet): `O1` `duplicates` (same `records.subject_key`, or cosine >= 0.9 with the same `embed_model`, content overlap >= 0.6, different subjects never, the older note not reworded and `unsupported(old, [new])` empty) supersedes the older with `SqliteLongTerm.set_status`; `O2` and `O3` read `sleep_turns(chats, since)` (chat and front turns that finished after `meta.sleep_until` and `forgotten_at`, completed, not undone, with a `turn.memory` event; `remembered` and `unsaved_claim` from it) through `recoverable` (`records.statements` not covered by the turn's notes, `records.newer_turns` drops a turn a newer one replaced, `unsaved_claim` turns first) and `_allowed` (`sensitive`, `unsupported`, `wrong_owner`; a note of the subject is superseded only when `subject_key` is equal, the note is older than the turn and the value differs) and write with `records.write(origin="sleep", created_at=<turn start>)`: `admitted_by` `sleep`, store source `sleep`, provenance `{source, run_id, session_id, turn}`; never a delete. A run that hit the cap leaves the watermark. The run's ids (no text) are saved in `index.db` `sleep_runs` by `run`'s `finally` through `asyncio.shield` (`_save_run`), so a failure, a stop or a cancel (re-raised) keeps its undo log and a run that changed nothing saves none; `sleep_until` is set only when the run completes; `ChatMemory.sleep` then drops the corpus's record items on a cancel (dropped by a real forget-everything); `sleep.undo` restores superseded rows and deactivates sleep-written rows (`superseded`, reason `undone: sleep <run_id>`, `removed` counts deactivations), leaving (`kept`) a written note a later note replaced or the user reworded. An undo sticks: for each pair a kept-note change (O1, O2b) separated, `undo` lists each note in the other's provenance `kept_apart` (`SqliteLongTerm.set_provenance`, active rows only), and a RETIRE it reversed lists the note's own id (do not retire again); `sleep.separated(a, b)` is true when either lists the other, and `duplicates`, `replaced_by` (so `replacements` and the model's `_replace`) skip such a pair, a model RETIRE of a note that lists itself is `noop`; a third newer note still replaces the restored one. Sleep never removes `kept_apart`; `ChatMemory.edit_record` calls `sleep.clear_kept_apart` (the note's own list and its id on every other note's). A written note an undo removed (O2, O3, O4, ADD, UPDATE) is an inactive negative (`session_entries(undone_only=True)`); `undone_before(store, turn, text)` (same session, same `provenance.turn`, same `_text_key` of the text: casefold, one spacing, no closing punctuation) makes `_tidy` skip the candidate and the model pass `noop` it, since a run that was capped, cancelled or failed leaves its turns unread and the next run would write it again; `forget_session` removes the negatives. Inactive rows are excluded from recall/tool/list. User forget hard-deletes: delete-one includes linked undone versions, forget-all clears all rows, `forget_session` purges inactive undone examples but keeps active notes, and `forget_chat_notes` clears all chat versions. Notes it writes have no vector until `melo memory reindex`. `model`/`model+tags` now run rules then a checked model pass: at most twelve chat requests total (including O4), temperature 0, eight-second timeout; per turn send typed text, previous completed user turn and top six active notes from normal ranking. Oldest-first for `model`; `unsaved_claim`, remember request, nearby remembered change, later-used items, oldest-first within each tier for `model+tags`. `_stale` guards rules and model writes against later typed retractions/replacements, including processed turns. Exclude any non-empty `origin` with `is_owner_question` (including `ask_owner` and `user_rule`); before every chat or embedding request `_check(lock, is_active, lock_self)` stops the run (`aborted` `stopped: gpu_lock` or `stopped: user_active`, saved and undoable) when `[memory] sleep_lock` exists, else when `[scheduler] gpu_lock_file` is held by another holder than `lock_self` (`sleep.lock_held`, read only), or a turn of any session kind started after `began` (`ChatMemory.sleep(began=None)`: now); `rules` with no embedding backend never reads the lock. JSON `ADD|UPDATE|RETIRE|NOOP`; quote must be in typed, values/owner/secret checks apply, UPDATE must match the write rules' target, RETIRE needs negation + shared content + `unsupported(old.text, [quote])` empty and logs the quote. O4 changes only the opening pronoun to a name supported by source/previous typed words. User edits are protected unless typed evidence is newer than edit time; unknown edit time remains protected. Report adds `refused` and `ms`. `processed` lists completed `[session_id, turn]` ids; `index.db.sleep_processed` keeps replay and per-note O4 completion across undo, pruned at 14 days; unfinished O4 remains eligible independently of turn replay. Use `split_thinking` before JSON parsing. Persist unreadable/timeout counts: first failure stays pending; second completes with `{session_id, turn, reason:"parse", note_id?}` in `refusals`. Unselected turns resume later; watermark stays just before the oldest pending finish. Drop replay candidates older than 14 days. An abort/change cap leaves the watermark unchanged. `POST /api/memory/sleep` accepts optional strict integer `budget` 1–100 only with `[ui] mode="developer"`; otherwise retain default 12 (also when test `dev_routes` is enabled). CLI has no override. RETIRE undo compares active ids/edit stamps with the run's baseline: unchanged preexisting conflicts are restored; later conflicting rows or edits are kept. No session carries a `memory.sleep` event, so the report is the return value, logged as `memory.sleep`. `POST /api/memory/sleep` (body `{variant?}`) and `DELETE /api/memory/sleep/{run_id}` answer 404 unless `[ui] mode = "developer"` or `ConsoleOptions.dev_routes`; `melo memory sleep [VARIANT]` needs developer mode (exit 2 otherwise). Idle sleep (`support/gateway/console/idle_sleep.py`, `Console.idle_sleep`, started by `Console._try_open`, closed by `aclose`; `ConsoleOptions.idle_sleep = IdleSleepOptions(clock, poll_s=60, idle_s=1200, spacing_s=21600, lock_present, pmset)`): every `poll_s` `IdleSleep.tick()` runs `ChatMemory.sleep(None, chats=store, began=...)` (`began` is the clock read before the first gate, so a turn that starts while the gates are read still stops the run) when all of these hold, tested in this order: `[memory] sleep` is not `off` and memory is on (`off` reads nothing); the store is open; `index.db` `meta.idle_sleep_at` (set before the run, so a failed run waits too) is at least `spacing_s` old (written only when a run starts; a stamp up to `CLOCK_BACK_S` = 24 h ahead of the clock, a clock set back, still blocks, a stamp further ahead is a wrong clock and the next run replaces it); the `[scheduler] gpu_lock_file` does not exist (`read_lock_file(...).present`, whoever holds it, never written; an empty `gpu_lock_file`, the default, is no lock reader, so this gate passes); none of the newest 100 chat and front sessions of the gateway is `busy` or has `updated_at` within `idle_s` (a turn's start and end set it; a terminal chat with `-c`, `-u`, `-r` or `[cli] chat = local` and workers outside the gateway are not seen); no task is `queued`, `running`, `held` or `parked`; `parse_battery(pmset -g batt).on_ac is True` (a failed read is no). `IdleSleep.blocked` holds the last reason (`off|store|spacing|lock|active|tasks|battery`). After a run `routes_memory.identity_changed` runs; with at least one change the main chat gets one echo `{echo: "sleep", run_id, count, variant, line, said, items: [{change, text}] (at most 5, text at most 120 characters, `change` `merged|updated|added|reworded|retired|changed` from `O1|O2|O3|O4|RETIRE`), more?}`, none: a log line only. `POST /api/front/echoes/{id}` `{do: "undo"}` on it (any other `do` is 400; 409 `sleep_running`, `errors.sleepRunning`, at once while `IdleSleep.running`, since the notes are locked and a wait would hold every other tap) calls `undo_sleep(run_id)` in every UI mode (an unknown or undone run changes nothing and answers 200 with an `undone` echo `{of, run_id}` worded `front.echo.sleptGone`, so the line settles and `/memory undo` goes on to an older one) and adds `{echo: "undone", of, run_id, line, said}`: `front.echo.sleptBack`, `sleptSome` (some notes `kept`) or `sleptNone` (all kept). Console: `static/main-chat.mjs` mark `☾`, `echoActions` gives Undo, `sleepNodes` folds the items; `/memory undo` is the page's `undoSleep` move (the newest unanswered `sleep` echo among the main chat's last 10 turns, from any chat). Terminal: `echo_line` appends ` · /memory undo`, `MainChat.undo_sleep()` taps the same echo (`GatewayClient.tap`), and the recap shows an unanswered one newer than the last turn.
- Memory ingest, for memory tests (`melo memory ingest FILE [-j] [-X notes=rules|none] [-X ingest=turns|compress]`, developer mode only: else exit 2; `support/memory/ingest.py`): loads `{"sessions": [{"id", "title", "date", "turns": [{"role": "user"|"assistant", "text", "date"}]}]}` as ordinary `chat` sessions through the gateway `SessionStore` with each turn stamped at its own time (`date` is ISO 8601, no zone = local time, or epoch seconds; a turn without one takes the session's + 1 s per turn), oldest session first, no chat-model call unless `-X ingest=compress` (memory items, below). A user message + the assistant message after it is one turn (a user message with no reply: empty answer; a second assistant message in a row continues the reply; an assistant message with no user before it, or with no text: skipped). Every turn is indexed in batches of 16 (`created_at` = the reply's time; the embedding model when set, else words only; `docs` counts chunks; a turn longer than 8 chunks hold is counted in `cut`); unless `-X notes=none`, `records.statements(user text)` become notes at the user message's time and get vectors when a model is set. Exit 2: bad file or option, file over 500 MB; exit 1: the console or app owns the chats. `-j`: `{sessions, turns, docs, notes, embedded_chars, cut, skipped, trimmed, seconds, model, error, ids}` (`ids` maps each file `id` to its store id). Docs: `docs/reference/cli.md`.
- `LOCALMELO_NOW` (developer setting for memory tests; ISO 8601, no zone = local time, or epoch seconds): while valid, `melo.clock.now()` is that instant, read by the model's `Date:` line and by recall's age decay; unset, empty or invalid (one warning): the wall clock. Session and turn times of new chats stay on the wall clock.
- Sleep diagnostics/fact guard: O3 and model ADD require a fact to be missing. An active note holds it only with every nonempty `records.value_terms` value (a changed value is a different fact whatever the cosine; with no evidence texts every CJK term is a value), the same polarity (a negation in both texts or neither), no known different subject, and cosine >=0.85 (`HELD_COSINE`) on comparable vectors, otherwise stemmed non-value `note_terms` overlap >=0.5. One candidate embedding cached per text, 1.5 s, lock/activity checked first; timeout/error uses words. The numbers `{note_id, coverage, subject_same, polarity_same, cosine, overlap, held}` are kept in `Change.guard`, `skipped` (rules) and the proposal's `guard`. Normal O2 changed-value updates remain. `selected` = `[session_id, turn]` per actual model request (including O4 repeats/failures), `processed` = completed replay. `proposals` = `{session_id, turn, op, note_id, target_text, text, quote, verdict, guard}` per op, text/quote/target_text <=200 and secret-redacted. Verdict `applied|noop|refused:<check>`; checks `quote_not_in_text|sensitive|first_person|unsupported|wrong_owner|stale|decide_mismatch|not_newer|self_target|no_negation|no_shared_term|edited|parse` (`self_target`: the note named was written from the proposal's own turn); cap-skipped ops are noop with capped=true. Model prompt lists notes `#id (date) text`, UPDATE/RETIRE name the older note, optional `topic` as the `remember` tool's. O2b: `replacements(active, sources)` (rules, S1 and up, after O1, no model call; own notes only, newest keeper first, prefilter equal `_subject` or content overlap >= `SUPERSEDE_OVERLAP`) supersedes the older note of a subject with another value by the newer one via `sleep.replaced_by` (neither user-edited, older by source-turn time, same owner, equal `subject_key` after a leading new/current/latest/updated or a `records.decide` UPDATE, each side with a value the other lacks; `_stale` uses the same normalized key); `Change(op="O2b", before_ids, after_id=keeper)`, quote of the keeper, nothing written, counted in the 20-change cap; undo (`KEEPER_OPS` = O1, O2b) restores only the older notes. The model path reaches it too (an UPDATE naming that note itself, or whose text a newer active note holds: every value, same polarity, same subject, or for an update that would be written as a copy every word of it plus a non-value word in common with the older note; nothing is written); a proposal about a note an O2b of the run retired is `noop`. O1 and O2b add the superseded notes' `[session_id, turn]` (and their own `replaces`) to the kept note's provenance `replaces` (`SqliteLongTerm.set_provenance`), so recall drops the old exchange (`recall.replaced_turns`, `current_only`); `Change.replaces_before`/`replaces_after` record it and undo removes only what the run added. A model ADD or UPDATE text with `I`, `me`, `my`, `mine`, `myself` or `我` outside quotes is `refused:first_person` (the prompt asks for "you" and "melo"). Sleep-written notes are never pinned (`pinned_quotes`), recall may list them. Synthetic PARSE on each parse/timeout; INVALID for malformed op. Applied Change carries verdict and identical proposal (null for rules); `refusals` remains terminal parse retries. No export/training.
- Recall settings (developer settings, `-X memory.KEY=VALUE`, `option_tiers.EXPERIMENTAL_KEYS` `#349`): `[memory] recall_records` (default `3`, 0-20) and `recall_docs` (`2`, 0-20) cap the notes and chat turns in a chat message's recall block, `recall_chars` (`4000`, `900` before #349, 200-8000) its size; `recall_notes` = `on` | `off` (`off`: no notes in the block, none pinned (`pinned_quotes()` is empty), turns only; `remember` and `search_memory` unchanged); `search_when_empty` = `off` | `hint` (`hint`: a block with no recalled item ends with the fixed line `service.SEARCH_HINT`, and the `turn.memory` event has `search_hint: true`). `recall_min_cosine` (`0.55`, 0.20-0.95) and `recall_min_coverage` (`0.6`, 0.10-1.00) are the bars an item must pass (least cosine, least share of the question's content words) in the automatic block and in `search_memory` (`recall.ranked(..., coverage=, min_cosine=)`). `recall_item_chars` (`900`, `234` before #349 and still valid, 120-2000; the user's words first, in a room of 234 or more at least as far as the plain 240-character head showed them) is the room one recalled chat turn takes in the block and in `search_memory`'s list, and `recall_excerpt` = `head` | `match` (`match`: each part of a turn shows the window of sentences that hold most of the question's content words, `…` where cut; `recall.Shown`, `recall.turn_said(text, show)`). `recall_form` = `excerpt` | `list` (`#428`, default `excerpt` = everything above): `list` shows each chat turn in the block and in `search_memory` as one line `[t<doc id>] <date> · <chat> · “<title>” · <cosine, 2 decimals | words>` (title: first sentence of the user's words, 80 characters at most; ` (older; …)` on a replaced turn), under the line `recall.LIST_GUIDE` ("Older chat turns that may hold the answer, closest first. Open the ones you need with open_memory before you answer from them; a title is not the content."), notes unchanged (`recall_records` bounds them); every turn that passes the bars is listed, best first, `recall_list_max` (`20`, 1-50) at most, no per-chat cap, and `recall_docs`, `recall_chars`, `recall_item_chars` and `recall_excerpt` do not apply to it; `search_memory`'s `k` may reach `recall_list_max`. With `list` the chat also has the read-only tool `open_memory(ids)` (1 to 5 ids such as `t123`; each returns the whole turn, every chunk joined, as `the user said “…”; melo replied “…”` with its date and chat, up to `recall_open_chars` (`4000`, 500-16000) characters, cut at a sentence end and ending `… (cut)`; an unknown or deleted id, a note id or a turn the chat still shows opens nothing and gets one line); the `excerpt` form's tool list is unchanged. Invalid values are config errors; `ChatMemory.recall_settings()` reads them each turn.
- Excerpt open (`#428`; the key stays a developer setting, `[memory] excerpt_open` = `on` (default) | `off` (the comparison: block, search result and tool list without ids and `open_memory`), `-X memory.excerpt_open=off`, saved only when `off`): for the excerpt form of turns only (no effect with `recall_form = "list"` or `recall_source = "items"`). With `on`, a chat turn's line in the recall block and in `search_memory` starts with `[t<doc id>] ` when it shows less than the whole turn: `recall.turn_excerpt` cut what the user said or melo replied (or left the reply out), or the document is a later chunk of a long turn (`Item.chunk > 0`), or the head of a turn that has later chunks (`Item.more`, set by `ChatMemory._sync`); a turn shown whole and every note read as before. The prefix is counted in the line's room (the shared text room is the prefix length shorter) and in `recall_chars`. When a line has an id, `recall.CUT_GUIDE` ("A line that starts with an id such as [t123] is cut; open it with open_memory when the answer may be in the rest.") follows the excerpts (one line, counted in `recall_chars`; last unnumbered line of a search result), `search_memory`'s description ends with the same sentence, and the chat has the read-only `open_memory` (same tool as the list form: ids `t123` or `[t123]`, one to five, whole turn up to `recall_open_chars`, a chunk's id opens the whole turn). `turn.memory` `used`/`searched` `shown` keeps the exact line, id included; `opened` as for the list form.
- Memory items (developer settings, `#428`; `support/memory/hippo_encode.py`, `hippo_route.py`, `melo/memory/hippo/policy.py`): `melo memory ingest FILE -X ingest=compress` has the chat model read each ingested chat in windows of `[memory] compress_at_chars` (`12000`, 4000-60000) characters (one exchange longer than that is read in at most 4 part windows of that size, `MAX_PARTS`, each after the first starting `[n] (continued) `, and only text after the fourth part is cut), one request per window at temperature 0 (thinking off where the backend takes it: `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking = false` for `vllm`, `sglang` and a `-u` server, `think: false` on Ollama's native API, nothing for `mlc` and cloud backends, the rule of `support/providers/llm/thinking.py` that step reviews share; the reply cached by model and prompt in `[memory] compress_cache`, `""` = `<memory dir>/compress_cache.jsonl`; `[memory] compress_parallel`, 1-8, default 1, sends the windows of all the chats of one ingest together through one shared semaphore of that size, `-X memory.compress_parallel=N` after `melo memory ingest FILE` for one run: each chat's result is built in window order and routing stays serial, chat by chat, so the items are the same and only the time changes; an unreadable reply that ran out of room, reported completion tokens at least `MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS - 16` or, with no usage, an unclosed JSON object, is not asked again but its window is split in two, between exchanges or, for one exchange, at a paragraph break, sentence end or whitespace near the middle, the second half starting `[n] (continued) `; each half is asked and cached as a window, a half that runs out splits once more, so a window makes at most 4 sub-windows, and a window under `MIN_SPLIT_CHARS` = 1500 fails instead; the window is cached as a `{"split": true}` row under its own second key, so a rerun makes no call; a half that fails fails alone; `PROMPT_VERSION` and the prompt and cache key of a window that neither splits nor is a part are unchanged, so an existing cache is served), and write memory items `{title, text, kind: profile|semantic|episodic, sources}`; a lasting statement no item covers becomes a `profile` item by the rules.
