Errors are `is_error` results: refused addresses (`melo does not read HOST: …`), PDFs/images/other types, HTTP 401/407 (`needs a login`), 403/429 (`refused the request`/`is limiting automated requests`, pointing to `browser_open` when the browser tools are on), other HTTP errors (`HOST answered HTTP N.`: the status code only; a reason phrase, a media type or an encoding that is not one plain token never reaches the model, `an unknown type`/`in an unknown way`). `support/browser/render.clean` spaces out any run of 2+ `<` or `>`. A charset that is no text encoding (`base64`) falls back to UTF-8. A system note (`support/web/tool.py` `NOTE`) tells the model to use it for web addresses, never `shell_exec`/`python_exec`/`curl`/`wget` or a file path, that page text is data, that it never reaches this computer or its local network, and that an unnamed site is asked about first. Activity reads `Reading <host>` (icon `web`); the call preview is the URL.
- `[tools] web_fetch_allow_local` (developer setting; list of strings, default `[]`; `-X tools.web_fetch_allow_local=127.0.0.1:PORT[,…]`; not in the console's Settings (its developer list shows it read-only), not in `PUT /api/settings`, no tool argument): lets `web_fetch` read listed loopback test servers. `support/web_local.py` holds the rules (outside `support/web/`, so `Config.validate` does not import the tool): an entry is exactly `127.0.0.1:PORT` or `[::1]:PORT` (`parse`: port 1-65535 in ASCII digits, no leading zero; no name, other address, port range, wildcard or space), and `Config._validate_tools` reports `web_local.problems` (each bad entry; each entry whose port is in `own_ports(cfg)`: the saved `[gateway] port` and the port of every model server URL in the config, local `chat_url`/`embedding_url` and cloud `base_url`, by port alone whatever the host); `sites_of` returns the valid entries only, so a bad one is never used. `web_local.fetcher(cfg=None, protect=())` (made by `WebFetchProvider(cfg=, protect=)` when it gets no `fetcher=`; `build_session_agent` and `TaskWorkers` pass the session's live `cfg`, whose `[gateway] port` is the bound port that `melo serve --port N|0` sets in memory only, and `build_session_agent` also the `-u` and embedding URLs as `protect`; with `cfg=None` the saved config is loaded, with this run's `-X`; the list and the config's ports are read when the provider is made, so a chat or task started later sees a changed file, and a model server in neither the config nor `protect` is not protected) gives `WebFetcher(allow=LocalAllow(sites, protected))`, or a plain `WebFetcher()` with no valid entry. `guard.LocalAllow.allows(host, ip, port)` is true only for an address written in the URL (`host == str(ip)`, never a name that resolves to it), loopback, `(host, port)` listed, and the port not in `protected()` (`own_ports(cfg, urls, running=True)`, evaluated at each check; `running` adds the port of the running gateway from `gateway_endpoint.read()`); `check_url(url, allow)` and `checked_addresses(.., allow)` ask a `LocalAllow` through `allows` and any other hook as before (names only, never a written address). `WebFetchProvider._admit` (the site gate) never reads a listed address at once for the user's words: `WebFetcher.listed(target)` skips the `names_host` shortcut, so the question `browser:<origin>` is asked whatever the user's words name; with no approval policy (`--yolo`, an unattended run, a task too) a listed address is read (nobody can be asked, and the developer listed it). In Auto, `_step_review.local_address` (an address written as a number that is not public, also as `host:port`) makes `StepReviewer.names_host` false and `plain_page_key` empty for it, so the model reviews each URL by itself and no verdict is shared across the server's pages. `WebFetcher._follow` checks every hop with it: a listed address may redirect to a listed one, an unlisted port is refused, and a hop that is not itself a listed address cannot redirect to one. `support/browser/` never imports any of it and passes no hook to the guard. Mark: `WebFetcher.fetch(local=cb)` calls `cb(target)` for each hop only a `LocalAllow` let through, after the checks and `admit`; `WebFetchProvider` then sets `TOOL_MARKS["allowed_local"]` (`melo/contracts/tools.py`; a dict `Agent._do_execute` makes per call while events are on), which becomes the optional `tool.finished.allowed_local = true`, and appends `web_local.NOTE` to the result or the error text; while a valid entry exists `system_notes()` ends with `web_local.MODEL_NOTE`. `melo config keys|get|set` print `settings.WARNINGS[key]` on stderr. The shell review (`melo/checker/review/shell.py` `_settings`, keys in `LOOSENING`, which a test keeps equal to `settings.WARNINGS`) makes a `shell_exec` or `python_exec` call that runs melo (`melo`, `python -m localmelo`, after wrappers) with `config set KEY` or `-X`/`--set KEY=…` on such a key a `self` finding (asks every time, never granted, refused in Auto), and a key built at run time (`$K`, a glob) undecided.
- `web_search` (`[web] search`, default `false`, not written when false; `-X web.search=true`; `melo config set web.search true`; Settings → Chats and folders → **Web search**, `PUT /api/settings` `web_search`; developer keys `[web] search_order` (list of `bing-rss`|`browser`|`baidu`, default `[]` = `bing-rss, browser, baidu`) and `[web] search_count` (1-8, default 6); #468; `support/web/search.py`, `search_pages.py`, `search_tool.py`): a provided tool, group `web`, tier `read` (`readOnlyHint`), that every chat and every console task gets only while the switch is on (`build_session_agent(web_search=False)` default; direct runs, `--brief` workers and the benchmark never get it: the bench key is `[web] search`, off unless `-X web.search=true`). Takes `query` (<=300 chars sent, whitespace collapsed) and `count` (1-8). `WebSearcher.search` tries `[web] search_order` (default `bing-rss` = Bing's `format=rss` feed by `WebFetcher` with its honest User-Agent and address guard; `browser` = `html.duckduckgo.com/html/` read by `BrowserToolProvider.read_for_search` (`support/browser/provider.py`: under the provider lock, in a tab of its own that is closed in `finally`, the chat's tabs and current tab restored; it runs the provider's own `addresses.require_public` before the load and `_read_tab` checks after (landing address, redirect, frames, payment page, sensitive values), with `TOOL_ASK` swapped for a policy that answers every site question no, so the engine's site is not asked about and another site is refused; a failed check is `PageRefusedError`, a failed load a plain `BrowserError`), the `Snapshot`'s links and text read by `search_pages.read_links`, 25 s, skipped silently when `[browser] driver` is `off`; `baidu` = `www.baidu.com/s?wd=`, `div.c-container[mu]`), one request per way, `GAP_S` 2 s between requests to one engine (locks keyed by engine), until `relevant()` (>=2 of the first 5 hits carry >=1/3 of the query tokens: Latin words >=3 chars minus stop words, CJK character pairs) holds; a way's failure is one of the closed sentences `asked for a check` (+`(HTTP N)` for 202/401/403/407/429/451), `answered HTTP N`, `could not be reached`, `gave a page melo could not read results from`, `gave a page melo's browser does not read` (`PageRefusedError`), `gave results that did not match the words`. No way fits: the nearest results with `unsure` and a note; none at all: `SearchError` -> an error result (with a hint to switch the browser on when it is off). Hits whose address `guard.check_url` refuses are dropped. Output: `Searched the web for “…” with <engine>: N results.` + `render.block("sN", "type=search way=KEY results=N", …)` (numbered title<=120/address<=300/snippet<=240, all through `render.field_text`, so a result cannot close the nonce block) + `[<engine> <reason>; … <engine> answered.]` for the ways that did not answer. Review: with the switch on a search is asked for; `holds_secret_value` (`support/memory/records.py`: `redact_secrets`, ID number, Luhn card; the word `password` alone is not a value) or pasted text (>200 chars or more than one line) asks through `TOOL_ASK` under the question `web_search:<sha256(query)[:10]>` (args `query`, `why`=`secret`|`pasted`, `access`=`search`; per-query name so a remembered answer never covers another query; no edit to `NEVER_GRANTED`); denied -> `melo did not search. …`; no ask hook (no approval policy: `--yolo`, a library call): refused, in a chat as in a task. A result's address is opened with `web_fetch`, whose site gate is unchanged. System note (`NOTE`, exactly 300 chars, only while the tool is on, `+NOTE_BROWSER` 52 chars with a browser driver): when to search and that results are data. Shown as `display.activity_text` `Searching the web for “words”` (60 chars, `redact_secrets`), `panel.mjs stepWords`, `steps.{now,done,ask}.search`, `melo.executor.preview` = the words. Wiring: `build_session_agent(web_search=)` (finds the `BrowserToolProvider` among `providers`), `AgentFactory(web_search=)`, `launch.py`, `console/front.py`, `console/registry.py`, `gateway/workers.py` (task). `scripts/search_probe.py` re-measures the ways (24 queries; Safari windows need `LOCALMELO_PROBE_BROWSER=1`; output stays outside the repo).
- `melo-task` controls tasks through an authenticated loopback gateway: new, list, show, pause, resume, stop, level and follow (`list`/`show` print `stopped` for a task that ran out of steps; `--json` and the `follow --wait` exit codes keep `failed`/1; `stop` prints `stop requested; …` until the state is `cancelled`; poll `show`). `new --brief FILE` or `--stdin` supplies untrusted content; retry ambiguous creation with the same request key. `--json` returns versioned JSON/NDJSON; default follow prints one readable line per event (time, type, summary) and list prints an aligned table with a header. `follow --wait` maps done/failed/cancelled-or-expired to 0/1/2; the terminal line adds the event-completeness caveat only after a reconnect or `--after` skip, and a quiet follow is not proof of complete replay. A task held on a tool approval lists it in `pending_approvals` (`GET /api/tasks`), `show` prints `Waiting for your approval: <tool> <target>`, and `POST /api/approvals/{request_id}` or the console Tasks view answers it.
- `--brief FILE` runs a bounded UTF-8 worker brief with a versioned JSON result; `--output-format stream-json` emits NDJSON events followed by a result. Agent construction errors, including refused config values and invalid TOML, report `startup_error`; output failures attempt `transport_error` but may prevent any final record. A broken startup-output pipe exits 1. Drain stdout, check exit and final result; startup error text is redacted and `$HOME` appears as `~`; a brief run appends a fixed worker-protocol paragraph to the brief, continues after any `continue` reflection whatever its flags say while steps and attempts remain, and adds a `no_change` notice plus a "Nothing has changed in the workspace yet" line at an attempt boundary where a git workspace is unchanged (ending with "Start with: <first next direction>"), the same notice with `scope: "step"` plus a "You have read for 6 steps…" line after 6 steps in a row without a workspace change, a tail note of tool output the window dropped (newest 8) on each planning request, and a reflection request that asks for paths with line numbers and the first command to run next (none of this without `--brief`); a brief's lines that start with `Check:` (rest of line = one shell command) are run by the harness as `shell_exec` calls (run in every `--builtins` setting, the model's own `shell_exec` calls unchanged; `--workspace` root and timeout apply) before the run ends `completed`: a failing check sends the model back with its command, exit code and last 60 output lines, at most twice (also once with exactly two steps of the last attempt left, when the workspace changed since the checks last ran), and the result's `tests` is `passed` or `failed` (items `source: "brief_check"` with `output_tail`: last 20 output lines, redacted, ≤4,000 chars; also `failed` when refused or still failing; the run still ends `completed`, exit 4 and a stderr line) with `brief_check` and `brief_check_failed` notices; explicit `--inbox FILE` reads complete instruction lines at planning boundaries and `inbox.accepted` offsets confirm live context insertion, not model receipt or cross-crash replay; `--inbox-fd N` reads the same lines from an inherited pipe whose read end is close-on-exec before tools start, so python, shell and MCP subprocesses cannot write it (recommended for untrusted tasks). A file inbox inside the workspace is refused as `setup_error` (exit 2, no model call); a file inbox is a steering channel, not a trust boundary, and same-user processes and tools can still write elsewhere. Acknowledgements wait for a slow reader instead of being dropped. Saved event text is redacted; session resume does not replay it. Redaction is pattern-based; arbitrary secrets may remain.
- Episodic digest recall prefers the same normalized task and workspace realpath; keyless digests are cross-task. `[retrieval]` has `cross_task_ratio = 1.1`, `cross_task_cap = 1` and `cross_task_cold = 0` (1 permits one cold cross-task digest). General memories bypass this gate. A digest without a checked `files:` or `verified:` line is not admitted; a later evidence-less attempt does not drop an earlier evidence-bearing attempt's digest. Delivered recall records and run stats report long-digest same/cross counts plus a task-local note count.
- Compress-mode heuristic notes extract up to 12 facts from visible replies without a note block, including bounded English negative/cancellation and Chinese residence/cancellation forms verbatim. Negative attribution requires the full assertion in the record; conflicting event times reject a match. This is heuristic: similar opposing detected polarities conflict rather than deduplicate; structured supersession is off by default. Python-only `AgentOptions(typed_assertions=True)` opts into narrow evidence-checked same-task updates and labelled historical recall; order comes from a timezone-aware record `timestamp`/`date` or per-task user message and sentence position (a restart does not link earlier user statements), only exact normalized duplicates stay ignored (different near-duplicates are kept), recall order uses wall-clock time, unlinked assertions remain unlinked and recall is relevance-limited. See [Memory](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/concepts/memory.md#reasoning-notes).
- Worker sessions: every direct run records one turn by default (`--no-save-session` or `[sessions] record_direct = false` opts out; `--save-session TITLE` titles it; `--parent-run ID` links a launcher); the web console Workers view follows an unfinished run on its event stream. `--import-session dsh-jsonl FILE [--title TITLE]` imports once by content hash. Read via `GET /api/sessions?kind=worker` (filters `status`, `source`, `parent_run`; `cursor` / `next_cursor`) and worker detail/turns, `GET /api/sessions/{id}/events` (follows an unfinished run by polling the file about once a second) and `/status`; no writes. `GET /api/sessions?kind=terminal` lists the chats of interactive `melo` sessions of the same file, read-only, served by id as worker runs are, with `kind` `terminal` and every text redacted on read (the terminal stores a chat unredacted); write routes return 404 for them. Workspace defaults to cwd; `session.tokens` is total tokens, `meta.usage` is the usage map; SQLite may create WAL/SHM sidecars on reads. Regex redaction is not a guarantee against arbitrary printed secrets; recognizable sensitive file reads are omitted. Thinking follows session retention.
- The web workspace has no Tasks link: a task opens in the activity panel beside the chat from its Activity row, a main-chat card or the address. `#/tasks/<id>` opens the panel on the task and leaves the chat in place; `#/tasks` opens the panel's list of all tasks (the Workers tab's "All tasks" link). "Back to Melo" or Escape returns to Melo's page, and after that the browser's Back does not reopen a task opened from the chat. The task page shows: state, recovery card as text, evidence status only when there is some, a finished task's answer first and its steps folded under "Steps" ("Live" only while it runs), Resume with a confirmation dialog only after 409 `confirmation_required`, Continue for a task that ran out of steps, task Stop via `PATCH /api/tasks/{id}` `{"state":"stop"}`, Pause ("Pausing…" until the task parks, then "Paused.") and a priority menu for a running or waiting task, and "Start again as a new task" when a started task has no card. See the console guide.
- Folders and workers: the main chat always works in `[gateway] workspace` (else `~/localmelo-workspace`) as it is now (its row only mirrors it; a changed default rebuilds its Agent on the same conversation; `PATCH` `workspace` on it is 409 `main_chat_folder`); a side chat keeps its folder. A task works in the request's `workspace`, else its `front_id` chat's (side chat: its folder; main chat: the default). An inherited folder the policy refuses (outside `~`, hidden, `~/Library`) creates the task already `failed` (`wait_reason` `invalid_workspace`, `folder_problem` says why, card line `Could not use its folder: …`), never run elsewhere; the task page offers Choose a folder. Activity task rows carry `folder`; a finished task's body has `not_committed`. A task continued by a message starts running with its own capture before its tools set up; if that run cannot start it ends `failed` with `wait_reason` `Could not continue: <why>` (one line, at most 160 chars), which its card line and activity `result` show instead of the earlier turn's reason. Workers get `file_edit` (exact single replace, asks, approval `target.diff`), `list_files`, `search_files` (a provided read-only tool in the task's folder) and `git_status` (status|branch|log|diff|show, argv-built, read-only, never asks, refuses paths or `REV:path` outside the workspace or naming a secret file; neither new built-in is in any mode default or `--builtins all`), tools with a per-task temp `HOME` (git identity and uv cache kept), and `AgentOptions.task_aids` (finish line two steps before the end; "The test environment refused: <cause>" before a tool text whose errors mostly share one environmental cause). A `python_exec` running only literal read-only commands through a module-level helper (`def run(*a): subprocess.run(list(a))`) is reviewed routine when every path-like argument (absolute, `~`, with `/` or `..`, git `-C`, `REV:path`, `--opt=path`) resolves inside the workspace (else undecided) and none names a secret file (`.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_rsa*`, `.netrc`, `credentials*`, `secrets*`, token files: high); git `-c`, `--ext-diff`, `--textconv`, `--exec-path`, `--upload-pack` or any option before the subcommand but `-C`/`--no-pager` is not read-only; a recursive grep (`-r`, `-R`, `--recursive`, `-d recurse`, combined short flags too), `git grep` and an rg naming no file or a folder are undecided (use `search_files`).
- Main chat: one session `kind=front` (`Main chat`) per gateway sessions file, made at console start, never deleted (`DELETE` 409 `main_chat`); every `kind=chat` session is its side chat; session bodies have `main`; `GET /api/sessions` adds `main` (body + `last_card`); `POST /api/sessions` makes a side chat; `POST /api/tasks` takes optional `front_id` (the starting chat; default the main chat). Side chat runs that end (cause `run`), tasks that end done/failed/expired, and pending approvals become `attention.card` events (no turn, never model context) in the main chat, `data` `{source_id, source_kind, title, state: done|failed|stopped|waiting|answered, line, at, request_id?}` (title at most 48 columns; `line`: two answer lines on done, the reason on failed, what is left on stopped (a task whose run ended `budget_exhausted`: stored `failed` with `wait_reason` `Out of steps`, `out_of_steps` true in its body, Continue = `POST /api/tasks/{id}/continue`), what is asked on waiting, the answer in words on answered, which follows its waiting card by `request_id` and is never `last_card`); the main chat's turns pages carry `cards`. The page opens the main chat, nests side chats by day, `⌘K` = New side chat, `Main chat ›` goes back; sidebar Workers is developer-only; worker runs are in the panel's Workers tab and linked from the empty main chat.
- Front (the main chat's turns): code first: `/task TEXT` or turn body `"as_task": true` starts a task; so does an imperative change to files it names (not a question); the rules read the first 4,000 characters of a text, and the task gets all of it; every task code starts begins at once under `short_title` of the text (`support/sessions/display.py`, the one function that names tasks and chats: first sentence of the first line (not a line of only a greeting, nor a leading code block), no opening please/请/帮我 or level word with a colon or comma (`no rush:`, `today,`, `今天：`), a path as its file name, at most 48 columns cut at a word with `…`, a question keeps its `?`; a chat's first title is the same), and, when the request is longer than a title, is renamed in 3-8 words in the request's language when the model answers (one background request at the lowest chat level, 6 s; a name the person gave meanwhile stays; otherwise the first words stay); "continue the … task" / `继续…任务` continues the one failed or stopped task whose title holds those words at once (several: one `suggest` echo each; a done or running one says so); a question that says briefly/in short/one line/简单说一下/一句话 is answered in the chat in at most two steps and never handed off; a short control phrase (stop/pause/resume/first, 停止/暂停/继续/先做) naming one open task changes it; a short follow-up word (finish/continue/commit/继续/提交…) naming one task, finished ones too, sends the message to it; all answer 200 `{"echo"}`. Other messages run `FrontAgent` (max 4 steps, no reflection, thinking off on oMLX/vLLM/SGLang, tools task_create/list/get/set_priority/control/message, search_files (read-only, 50 hits `path:line`, inside its folder), file_read, list_files, memory tools). `task_list` carries each finished task's first answer lines, `task_get` its whole answer (8,000 characters, then a cut line) and the files it wrote; each turn reads the tasks that ended since the last. A reply that only announces work ("I'll start by…", "我先…") is handed off like the step cap. `task_message` sends the person's own message: a running task reads it at its next step (`inbox.accepted`), a done/failed/stopped task continues in its own session as a new turn (`TaskStore.reopen`); only when the typed text names the task, or says a follow-up word about the newest task shown, else a `suggest` (`action` `send`). Echo `sent` (`how` queued|continued). Task level from the typed words only: urgency, a deadline today or a bare un-negated today/今天 → P1, no rush → P3, else P2, `level_source` computed. Not settled in 4 steps (a step whose every call a policy check or Auto refused does not count, at most 2 a turn: `AgentOptions.refused_steps`, `refuse_call`; the person's Deny, a timeout and the same refused call again always count) → by `start_rule`: `start` → `completed` + a task; `answer`/`offer` → one more request without tools (`Agent.closing_answer`) and its answer (`NO_ANSWER_TEXT` when none), plus "Start this as a task?" only for `offer` (a question: `?` anywhere, "quick question", not a polite request such as "can you …?" or 请…; or words that say not to act), never for a question code answers or a status question (`is it done?`, `跑完了吗`); the sentences are Chinese for a message with Chinese characters. A request in steps (`steps_request`: look at something outside the chat (a link, a file, a site, repo, folder, document or `my …`/`我的…`), then tell/list/write: `去…看一下…然后告诉我…`, `look at my site and tell me …`) starts like any request, even when its last step asks a question; not when what it looks at is a task, nothing outside (`看看天气然后告诉我`, `look at this and tell me`), or the message opens with explain/tell me/translate (解释/说说/讲讲/介绍/告诉我/翻译). Text after a colon to explain, translate or summarize (`翻译成英文：…`, `translate into English: …`) with no file or link is `answer`. `status_question` needs a state word and no verb that acts (`Is the report ready? If not, write it to report.md` is a question to offer), in a question or in words that name a task and ask to look or be told (`look at the slides task and tell me its progress`, `check the slides task …`); state words include what a task found or said (`what did it find?`, `has the task found …`, `what does the task say?`, `它找到了什么`, `任务发现了什么`; `What does report.md say?` is not one). Words against a task (`no need for a task`, `don't make a task`, `不用开任务`, `别开任务`) are `hands_off`. Control tools act only when the typed text (never an attachment) asks and names the task, else a `suggest` echo. A repeating phrase code can read (`every weekday at 8:30 …`, `每天早上九点 …`) answers a `chore` echo (`Run this every weekday at 8:30?`; no model call). A reminder cue with a time (`remind me to … on Friday at 9`, `in 2 hours`, `提醒我明天九点 …`; `记得`/`别忘了` only with a time) answers a `chore` echo with `reminder: true` and a `once` schedule (`Remind you on Fri Oct 30 at 9:00?`; `save` and `cancel` only); with no usable time it answers an `ask` echo with `ask: "when"`, and the next message that is only a time answers it. Echoes: `attention.echo` in the main chat (`echoes` on its turns pages); `POST /api/front/echoes/{id}` `{"do": undo|apply|start|level|save|once|cancel}` (the last three answer a `chore` echo). Levels read as P-codes in both modes (P0 runs first, P1 today, P2 normal, P3 when there is time, P4 only when idle, P5 on hold), with the meaning in menus and as a tooltip; the old words, `Pn` and numbers still parse everywhere (`level_number`), `melo task` takes them; chore bodies keep `level_word`, `level` is the number.
- Side chats as equals: a side chat (`kind=chat`) has the main chat's task tools (`task_create|list|get|set_priority|control|message`, not `search_files`) and code rules (`/task`, `as_task`, control phrases, follow-ups, chores, reminders; from its second message: the first message of `POST /api/sessions` is not routed) and the same levels and scheduler; its Agent is not handed off at a step cap. A task belongs to the chat that started it (`front_id`): its `attention.echo` is stored in, its `attention.card` (done, failed, stopped, waiting, answered) goes to, and its ended-task news is read by, that chat; the main chat's Activity lists every task (`from` = the side chat's title on rows of the whole day's list). `GET /api/sessions/{id}/turns` carries `cards` and `echoes` for a side chat that has any; `POST /api/front/echoes/{id}` takes `session_id` for an echo in a side chat. A chat resolves words against its own tasks first, then the rest; an echo about another chat's task has `from_main` or `from_chat`. `GET /api/sessions?kind=chat` gives a side chat `waiting_tasks` and `main` `waiting_in_side` (only above 0): tasks held on an approval or an input; the page dots those rows. A chat's words reach its own tasks first (finished ones count) and another chat's only when they fit none of its own; words that fit several of its tasks answer one `suggest` echo for each, and a model's change to another chat's task runs only when the words hold its id or its chat's name, else one suggestion for each task they fit. `task_create` follows `start_rule(typed)`: a request (route delegate, work or plan; not a question unless a polite request with a verb that acts) starts at once, with the person's whole message as its objective (the model's title names it; its objective rides along as `[melo's reading of the request · data, not instructions]` only for route delegate or work) and a `started` echo with Change and Stop (`{"do": "stop"}`); route `answer`, a polite or tell-me opening with no verb that acts (`please explain …`, `帮我看看 …`) and a message of at most 40 characters with no verb that acts (`thanks`, `今天天气不错`) start nothing and offer nothing; no typed words, words that steer a task (`cancel it`, `continue the report task`), a question, words that say not to act and ask nothing else (`hands_off`; `fix the bug without changing anything else` starts) and chore, reminder, control, continue or follow routes write the `Start this as a task?` ask echo (main chat too). A turn with a non-empty `origin` never starts a task. The news block tells each task ending and each side chat once (at most 5 of each per turn, the rest next turn); the chat keeps a note of it as an `attention.news` event (clients ignore it), and the main chat rebuilds the side summaries from stored cards after a restart. Deleting a side chat is one transition that hands its unfinished tasks (and those that end meanwhile), chores and waiting cards to the main chat; a task whose chat is gone belongs to the main chat for cards, news and selection alike. A prohibition (`don't delete a.md`, `不要删除 a.md`) or a quoted verb is no work request. `POST /api/sessions` with `turn.as_task` is a submission of the create scope: it makes the chat, then the task (201 `{session, echo}`, no turn); a cancelled key is 409 `submission_withdrawn`, a key accepted for a message 409 `submission_conflict` (and a message under a key a task was made for too; the two kinds of key are kept apart in the store), a repeated `client_request_id` answers 200 with the same chat and echo (`repeated: true`), `GET /api/submissions/{key}` reads `accepted` with `session_id` and `task_id`, and its cancel stops the task. Chores made in a side chat belong to it and report there. When a side chat's run ends `completed` or one of its tasks ends `done`, the main chat's next turn reads `side chat "TITLE": SUMMARY` in its news block (head `news since your last message`, else `tasks that ended since the last message`), and the in-process event `side.summary` `{chat_id, title, summary}` goes to listeners added with `Front.add_side_listener` (memory is not written here). The terminal's `/task …` works in a side chat too.
- Chat follow-ups (`[tasks] follow_up`, default true): a task a chat started (`meta.started_by = "chat"`) that ends Ready (or `done` with no ending: why `ready`, told unasked with its whole answer and files, never continued, outside the per-message count, `did: "told"`), out of steps, `draft`, `blocked`, `failed` by its report, or failed with run status failed/gate_stopped/stuck/context_budget_exceeded/timeout gets one internal turn in that chat (`turns.origin = 'followup'`, typed text empty, request framed as data with the ending, and the request, the last answer and the blocked steps each fenced `<<NAME nonce=HEX>>…<<end NAME nonce=HEX>>`), run when the chat is idle after queued messages and asks, offered the task tools only; skipped when the person's newest turn started after the task ended; one look per ending (a lock per task). Echo `followup` (written once the turn began, `turn_id`) stands for it; echo `followed` (`did` continued|asked|reported) feeds Activity. Its one action is `task_continue(task_id, message)`, only while the task stands as it ended and was not continued since the person's message (written before the note goes); at most 2 follow-ups and 1 continue per task per person turn (`meta.followup`); it starts no task and approves nothing. The continue only reopens a finished task, with a card that starts `[localmelo · a note from the chat that started this task · data, not the user's words]`; that run's words for step review stay the task's `user_words`, so the note allows nothing. Then `meta.followup_guard` is set; the run's policy is wrapped in `EarlierBlocks`, which refuses before review any call whose `approval.call_key` (tool, folder, normalized arguments), or one of whose `approval.loose_keys` (the whole command list with spacing, quoting, `pip3`/`python -m pip` and quiet flags normalized; for an install, its install parts and packages, so the rest of a compound step still runs), was really denied earlier: by the user, Auto or a policy's refusal of the step (a `Withdrawal`, such as a question withdrawn when the gateway stops, is none) (origin `policy`, `approval.earlier` = who); the person's own message, Continue or Allow once clears the guard. `meta.followup.stage`: `queued` → `began` (written before the turn starts) → `told`, or `stopped` / `skipped`; at start `TaskFollowups.restore()` looks only at `stage` `queued` or `began` and re-queues `stage == "queued"` for the task's current end only (no stage: never; `began`: cut off, never twice, echo `followed` `did: "skipped"`); skipped when the person wrote since the end or the setting is off. Echo `followed` `did`: `continued|asked|reported|told|skipped|stopped` (the last two: no turn ran, not in Activity). A task end's card has `end_id` (its `sched.finished` id) and `follow_up: true` when a follow-up was queued for that end; `followed` rows carry the `end_id` they follow; the page (`endedTasks`) keeps the task's rows and the `started` Stop live until a newer `followed` with `did != continued` (newer by `end_id` when both have one, else by time). Stop on the `started` echo stops the follow-up (under the task's lock, so one being queued is caught; queued: dropped; running: turn cancelled, `task_continue` refused; the current end kept with `stage: stopped`), then the task if it still runs; a finished task gets `Stopped: …`, with `undo: null` (no Undo) when no follow-up was stopped. A card's report is its own run's (`ending.turn`, else the newest `turn.started` before its `sched.finished`). A site question a tool asks while it runs (`TOOL_ASK`, `browser:<origin>`) that the user, Auto or a policy refused is kept in `tool.finished.tool_asks` (`call_key`, `loose_keys` with `ask:browser:<origin>` and `ask:site:<host>`: host in ASCII, lower case, no final dot); a question that got no decision is kept there too (`origin` `error` with the failure as `reason`, or `withdrawn`; no `preview`, no `call_key`): `approvals.ask()` is the one place any policy is asked, for a call, a folder and a tool's question alike; a guarded run refuses that question and any other on that host, whatever the scheme, port or spelling, before review or prompt, and web_fetch checks it before reading a host the request names. It also refuses a `shell_exec`/`python_exec` step that names a literal `http(s)://` address on that host (`review.site_keys`: each command word, each string of the code, an f-string whose host is written out; capitals, port, final dot, `%XX`, IDNA and IP forms normalized as `site_key` does; probe only, never stored with a blocked step); also a `curl`/`wget` positional address without a scheme (dotted host, never an option's value) in any shell syntax (`if`, `( )`, quoted `$( )` and backticks, `bash -c`, `bash <<<`, `eval`, `env -S`, line continuations, any wrapper before `curl`), curl proxy values and `*_proxy=`/`http.proxy=` words, every nested or percent-encoded `http(s)://` address, IPv4 in one-number/hex/octal form, and the literal host of `http.client`/socket/`pycurl` calls (Python imports resolved); a host built at run time (`$H`, `{h}`, `%s`, a variable from a file) gives no key, and while a site is refused such a step (`review.reaches_unread_site`) is `undecided` even when the rules call it routine (Auto or a grant), so the model reviews it, told the hosts refused in the task (`<refused>` block, hosts only, newest 5); a percent-encoded or international host that does not decode is refused while any site is (`ask:site-unreadable`). `denied_records` counts only real blocks (call key, no `earlier`).
- Workers ask their chat: worker tool `ask_owner(background, situation, problem, likely_causes, options, help_needed, if_unsolvable)` (all required, 1-600 chars; at most 3 per run) waits, holding no model call and never displaced, while the owner chat (`front_id`, else the main chat) runs one internal turn per ask when idle, oldest first (`turns.origin = 'ask_owner'`, schema 3; typed text empty; request framed as data; chat's mode and tools; 8 steps). The turn answers with `task_answer(task_id, answer)` or asks the person with `ask_person(task_id, background, what_happened, tried, choices, question)` (reply box: `POST /api/front/echoes/{id}` `{"do": "reply", "text"}`, or a message to the task; no time limit). No answer within 10 minutes of that turn's start, or a turn that ends without either: the worker gets `No answer from CHAT; go on with your best option and say so in your report`. Echoes in the chat: `task_ask`, `task_answered`, `task_escalate`, `ask_end` (`person|timeout|stopped|expired`), `queued`/`dequeued` (a message sent during an internal turn is queued, not 409, kept in the chat's `meta.queued` (accepted only once stored), and runs next, also after a restart, once (a turn already started under its key is not run again); the page's composer stays open). A timeout or a stopped task also stops the internal turn; after `ask_person`, `task_answer` is refused; a deleted chat's open questions move to the main chat; a restart expires the open row (the escalation once asked). The internal turn cannot be retried (409 `not_retryable`), is no consent for step review and no user statement for core memory (`run_task(from_person=False)`), carries `origin` on `turn.started`, has no `remember` (`hide_tools`), and memory keeps, indexes and quotes none of it (an answered question is kept once as the task's exchange, `ChatMemory.index_exchange`, never a note); the change feed and `export_turns` carry `origin`. The terminal shows a task's question as a muted `Task “TITLE” asks: PROBLEM` line, then the answer, then `→ melo answered “TITLE” · ANSWER` or `! “TITLE” needs your answer: QUESTION`, never the request's frame. With exactly one task waiting for the person in a chat, a plain message (not a question, work request, command or control phrase) answers it: echo `answer_sent` with Undo for 10 s, then `answer_delivered`; `/answer TASK TEXT` (page and terminal) names one when several wait; `task_escalate` has `waiting`. Task body `ask` `{ask_id, chat_id, chat_title, on: owner|person}`; Activity `Waiting on CHAT`/`Waiting on you`. In-process events `task.ask {task_id, ask_id, chat_id}` and `task.answer {…, by: owner|person|timeout}` (`OwnerAsks.add_listener`). `task_get` of a running task reads live: step of budget, last action, open question, last plan note. The internal turn never grants an approval.
- Task endings (fail closed): a finished worker run gets `ending` on the task (`TaskRecord.ending`, task bodies, Activity rows, task cards, the `sched.finished` event): `{state: ready|draft|blocked|failed|dropped, proposed, reasons[], question, tests[{command, exit_code, outcome}], uncommitted[], notes[], turn, run_id, at}`, decided by code (`task_endings.decide`) from the run's own paired tool events and the task folder's state (git, or outside git a bounded snapshot of its code files) since the first run after the task last ended ready (`tasks.work_base`; a git error is never kept, so only that run is unchecked); the report's last line `Ending: ready|blocked: <need>|failed|dropped` is only a proposal. A test is a plain runner command with no shell operators or newline (`python -m pytest -q`; also `uv run`/`poetry run`, npm/pnpm/yarn/bun, cargo/go/swift, `node --test`, `make test`, tox, nox, `npx jest|vitest`, `xcodebuild test`) or a `python_exec` of imports plus one `sys.exit(subprocess.run([...]).returncode)`, `subprocess.run([...], check=True)` or `subprocess.check_call([...])`; listing or collecting flags make it no test, a path outside the folder makes its result unknown, and anything else that starts tests has an unknown result. A writer is any call not known to read (git reads, `git add`/`commit`, prints, string methods are readers). Last test failed -> `tests_failed` after a change, else `tests_still_fail` (no Finish it); unknown -> `tests_unverified`; changed code (git: since the baseline, docs by extension only; outside git: code files, by extension or build-file name, the snapshot saw change, or a file tool's write to a code file anywhere) with no test after the latest writer -> `tests_missing`, with or without a test setup, except in a Finish it run (its message, `task_endings.finishes`, or the person's own message asking for the tests when continuing an ended task; never a first run or a run resumed after a park): with no test run that has a result it ends Ready noting `no_tests` when no setup applies or a whole pytest/unittest run (no `-k`, `-m`, `--deselect`, path or test id; strict test shape) collected nothing (exit 5), `tests_missing` when a filtered run found nothing or a runner said it ran no test (exit 0 and its own output says so: ctest `No tests were found`, phpunit `No tests executed`, mix `0 tests, 0 failures`, Django `Ran 0 tests`, cargo or Maven counts all 0), else `no_runner` (melo found tests here but could not run them, not owed); the Finish it mark is kept on the task (`tasks.finishing`) through a park and resume; and a Finish it run's ending never offers Finish it again (`finish_tried` marks an owed one); tests asked (`front_rules.asks_tests`, double negatives like "don't forget the tests" and "make sure the tests pass" included) with no change -> `tests_missing` where a setup applies, else note `no_tests`; test setups include Django, pytest in `pyproject.toml`/`setup.cfg`, CMake tests, phpunit, mix, Gradle/Maven `src/test`, .NET test projects, zig, cabal, deno, a justfile `test` recipe, a Makefile `check` target and a real `package.json` test script, each with its runner (`python manage.py test`, `mix test`, `phpunit`, `dotnet test`, `ctest`, `gradle|gradlew test`, `mvn test`, `make check`, `zig build test`, `cabal test`, `deno test`, `just test`); pytest/unittest exit 5 (no test collected) is no test; an asked commit (commit, push, PR, 提交, 推送) with changes dirty -> `commit_missing`; a file the words ask it to write or save (`write … to notes.md`, `保存为 report.csv`, objective, the person's words or a later message; `task_files.asked_files`) not in the folder (as written, or a bare name anywhere under it) -> `file_missing`, names in `ending.missing`, not owed; git or the snapshot failing, over 2,000 changed (outside git: code) files or over 40,000 files outside git, or `git stash list` grown in this run (or above where an earlier run that grew it started, until ready) -> `unchecked` while Finish it can still run a test or commit (not in a Finish it run), else `too_large`, `unreadable` or `stashed` (said plainly, no Finish it); git that cannot run = not a git folder; any reason -> `draft`; a question -> `blocked`; out of steps -> `draft` (`out_of_steps`); a worker's `dropped` reads Not needed. `POST /api/tasks/{id}/continue` also finishes a task that owes tests or a commit (`task_endings.can_finish`; `ending.finishMessage`/`ending.finishCommitMessage`). Other paths read the state's default (`dropped/stopped`, `failed/run_failed`).
- A task's approvals go through its chat (web console; memory only, per chat): a step the person allowed in a chat or one of its tasks runs again in that chat's later tasks without asking only on an exact code match (same tool, same step key: Python syntax tree / exact shell text / file path + content hash / files the rules read by digest, same resolved folder) when the call is reusable: tool `python_exec`, `shell_exec`, `file_write` or `file_edit`, review verdict `routine` by the rules, no category; approval `origin` `"earlier"`, echo `earlier` in the chat ("Used your approval from HH:MM", Revoke → echo `revoked`), task body `earlier` (`live`). A grant that holds in the owner chat (its own or the main chat's) covers its tasks' routine calls in Ask; these recorded steps live in memory only, grants do not. Such a task is reviewed with every file changed since its owner chat began (not since the task began); if that start cannot be read, no grant or earlier approval applies. Never: high-impact, `undecided`, model-settled or unreviewed steps; network, MCP and other tools the rules do not read; chores (`user_rule`) and any task whose `origin` is not `user` (`POST /api/tasks` / `melo task new` tasks are `user`, owned by the main chat); another chat's approvals; Auto's Allow once (never recorded); an Allow answered after its chat was deleted; revoked entries; a deleted chat's entries. Auto never runs a step it blocked on an earlier approval. Waiting approvals carry `remembered` (code says whether the Allow is kept; the card says so). A task's waiting approval shows in its chat's card with melo's explanation for origins `user` and `user_rule` only (one model call, 20 s, task title/goal + call + review reasons as data, never tool output; `explanation {state, text}`; decides nothing). An Auto task's blocked step gives its chat a card `state: "blocked"` with Allow once. Routes: `GET /api/approvals/{request_id}`, `DELETE /api/sessions/{id}/approvals/{entry_id}`, `GET /api/sessions/{id}/tools` `approvals`.
- Slash commands in the console and app: `GET /api/commands` is the terminal's command table with `help` in `en` and `zh-Hans`, `during_turn`, `keys` and the page `action`; the page's `/` menu and local rows (`static/slash.mjs`, `slash-actions.mjs`) run each command without sending it to a chat; `/task` and `/answer` are sent as the chat's own messages; `POST /api/sessions/{id}/undo` forgets the newest finished turn; `browser` on `PUT /api/settings` is `/browser on|off`; a message that starts like a command needs a space first (`//text` stays a message).
- Chores: a saved request on a schedule (`{kind: daily|weekdays, at: "HH:MM"}`, `{kind: hours, every: 1..24}` or `{kind: once, at: "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM"}`, a reminder: at most 366 days ahead, switched off after its run, `late_min` when it ran 5+ min late; a request starting `Reminder: ` runs as a restatement and its card is `reminder: true`), rows in the scheduler component (version 6; `chores`, `chore_meta`; an older file only gains the tables), each with a `revision`. A code-only tick every 30 s starts each due chore as a task (origin `user_rule`, `front_id` its chat, key `chore:<id>:<planned time>`), planning the next run from now plus up to 120 s jitter: a run missed while asleep happens once at wake, a chore whose last run has not ended skips its slot. Every 30 min the check-in looks (code only) for a finished chore run not yet reported or a task that waited a whole beat; with nothing, no model call and no card, else one model call and one `checkin` echo in the main chat; `PUT /api/checkin` `{on}` switches it. API: `GET|POST /api/chores`, `PATCH|DELETE /api/chores/{id}` (`revision`, 409 `stale_revision`), `POST /api/chores/{id}/run`. Panel: Scheduled tab; `#/scheduled`. See reference/api-v2.md#chores.
- Terminal main chat: bare `melo` (default `[cli] chat = "main"`) is a gateway client of the main chat: it uses the gateway `~/.cache/localmelo/gateway/endpoint.json` names (`{pid, host, port, instance, id, started}`, 0600, written by every gateway once it listens and holds the main chat, removed on shutdown; stale = dead pid or `GET /` without `X-LocalMelo-Gateway: ID`), else the one on `[gateway] host:port`, else the one holding `~/.cache/localmelo/gateway/sessions.db.owner` on its own port (found with `lsof`), else starts `melo --serve --host H --port P` in the background (log `~/.cache/localmelo/logs/gateway.log`; left running after melo quits; never a second gateway on the file). One line: `Started the gateway in the background on port N; it keeps running until melo serve stop.`, `Connected to the gateway on port N.`, or `⚠ No main chat (REASON); this is the terminal's own chat.` (then the old local chat). Turns go through `POST /api/sessions/{id}/turns` and draw from the chat's SSE stream; approvals use the terminal's list and `POST /api/approvals/{id}`; cards are one line (`✓ Done: TITLE · LINE  /chats opens it` or `melo task show ID`). Commands: `/chats` (list), `/side [title]`, `/main`, `/task TEXT`, `/retry` (`POST …/retry`), `/approvals ask|auto` and Shift+Tab (`PATCH /api/sessions/{id} {"approvals": …}` on the open chat; a side chat not made yet sends the pick in `POST /api/sessions`; `deny` and `forget` are the terminal's own chat's); `/model`, `/undo`, `/sessions`, `/attach` and the other local-file commands say they work in the terminal's own chat. `-X cli.chat=local` (or `LOCALMELO_CHAT=local`), `-u`, `-c`, `-r`, `--yolo` keep the local chat. The work zone and Ctrl+T show P-codes. `GET /api/sessions/{id}` has `last_event_id`; approval `review` has `categories`. Direct runs and workers unchanged.
- The web workspace offers `#/workers` (server-filtered and cursor-paged) and `#/workers/<id>` (read-only; an open unfinished run is read once and followed on `/events`, the list re-read every 3 s, no write controls; a Terminal chats chip lists `kind=terminal` chats, followed while a turn runs and again at the next turn). A started task's card in `#/tasks/<id>` shows a Live section: its session (the task id) read once with `/turns?events=true`, then a running or held task followed on `/events?after=<last id>` (a hidden tab keeps following, and a stream that ended is opened again after 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 then 30 s, by the one `followEvents` in `static/turns.mjs` that the chat and the Workers view use too; it closes after one last read when the task is done, failed, cancelled, expired, interrupted or parked); task events are shown as a chat's are, unredacted. Worker detail `tokens` is null without integer completion tokens; chat-only details and submission lookup return 404 for worker-only IDs. See the console guide and API v2 reference below.
- The `/` workspace shows a setup card while no model can answer and no chat is open: it calls `GET /api/setup/detect` (the first run's detection; `state` `found`|`needs_key`|`none`, `name`, `backend`, chat `models`, `loaded`, `suggested` (null: the user chooses), `problem`, `start` (how to start a server here: `name`, `commands`, `note`, `guide`)) only while shown (with `none` it shows the commands and asks again every 3 s, not in a hidden tab), and Use this model saves through `PUT /api/settings` (a `vllm` backend whose listing named oMLX is written `omlx`), tests and reads health; the composer is disabled meanwhile. It uses `/api` for connection settings, connection testing, a browser-local theme, tools/grants/memory/runs drawer (developer mode, saved as `[ui] mode` from the settings' Developer tab, adds an Events tab, memory internals and run counters; display only), earlier turns, failure controls and per-tab outbox recovery; its styles are tokens in `workspace.css` `:root` (colour as `light-dark()` pairs, a type scale with a 12px floor, four radii) that `tests/gateway/test_web_assets.py` enforces; console sessions use `RememberingPolicy` to ask before `file_write` and `python_exec` and render approval cards (`Allow once`, `Allow for this chat`, `Deny` + note; body unchanged; a `file_write` of text over an existing file shows what it replaces from `target.diff`: `added`, `removed`, `rows` of `{kind, line, text}` with secrets redacted, and `note`, a sentence when melo cannot compare; whole or absent, within 200,000 bytes and 1,000 rows; display only); a failed turn offers one next action per status (a model server that cannot be reached: `Could not reach the model server`, Try again, a `Change the server address` link, its raw error only under Details); Escape stops a running turn only with focus in the composer and closes what is open in every view; default mode (`[ui] mode` not `developer`, read from `GET /api/settings` at boot) hides, keeping every id, the level chip, Details, the GPU line, the LOCAL badge, the status row's cache, step, phase and queue segments, the task priority and the Workers and Tasks links until a run, terminal chat or task exists, names the model in the header chip, shows a banner while a chat waits on a foreign GPU lock (its turn reads `Waiting for this Mac's GPU` in both modes) and stacks the settings dialog (Model with its test, Appearance, Developer toggle); a new chat shows a folder chip (`#folder-btn`, `In <folder>`; the default is `GET /api/settings` `workspace`) with a panel of the default, up to four recent folders and Choose a folder (a path field in a browser; in the macOS app the `localmeloFolder` message handler's system panel) and one-line starters (`#starters`), and `POST /api/sessions` carries the pick as `workspace` (absent for the default); a chat's header and sidebar row name its folder, an accent dot marks a chat waiting for approval, and on a phone or touch screen the keyboard hints and the model chip (while it only names the model) are hidden and a failed turn's next steps are 44 px buttons; developer mode shows all as before; legacy `/v1` has no approval policy.
- Console Settings (`static/settings.mjs`): a vertical tablist of sections (Model server, Memory, Chats and folders, Scheduled, Appearance; Developer in developer mode only), the section beside it (a sheet at 700 px or less). Each change saves alone and offers Undo: `PUT /api/settings` with the loaded revision and only that field (`across_chats`, `memory_retriever`, `workspace`, `mode`, `language`, `approvals`, `web_fetch`; 409 `settings_changed` asks for a reload), `PUT /api/checkin`, the theme in `localStorage`, or the macOS app's `localmeloDesktop` handler for Melo on the desktop (hidden in a browser). The connection form is saved with **Save connection**. `GET /api/settings` adds `memory_retriever`, `developer_settings` (every key `melo -h all` lists, by section, with `value`, `default`, `flag`, `issue`, `file`) and `run_options`; a failed `POST /api/settings/test` adds `failed` (`chat` or `embedding`). Docs: guides/web-console.md#settings.
- Saved terminal chats: `melo -c` resumes the newest eligible chat in this workspace; `melo -r [ID|TITLE]`, `/sessions [filter]` and `/resume [id|title]` resolve or pick one. Picker filtering, Tab folder/all-folders and Esc preserve the draft. Startup selection precedes the banner; the recap names the chosen chat. Exit prints `melo -c` when the chat is the newest of the folder melo ran in, else `melo -r ID`. Resuming keeps current model/workspace and `/verbose`/`/thinking`, brings that chat's grants back and explains restored memory (`[sessions] resume_mode = "pairs"` default or `"window"`); `/retry` keeps stored typed text and `/expand` reads persisted tool output. Cross-window changes reload before sending; busy/deleted sessions keep drafts. Only CLI chats with finished turns are offered; no web/scheduler sessions. `-c` and `-r` are mutually exclusive and interactive-only. Direct parsing/output stays unchanged; put task text after `--`.
- Interactive text attachments: `/attach PATH` (quote spaces), `/attachments`, `/detach N|all`; explicitly select an `@` file completion, not typed prose. Idle only; detach before switching sessions. Workspace regular UTF-8 text only: no symlinks, traversal, URLs, recognized secret files, binary or images. Max 8, 256 KiB each, 512 KiB total original bytes; composed prompt limit also applies. Redaction is best effort; changed snapshots are shown for confirmation. Session snapshots are stored unencrypted; `/retry` uses the stored snapshot, not the file. Pairs resume has a 32,000-character user/answer budget and may omit a turn; window can omit it too. See [terminal guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/terminal.md#attach-text-files). The slash-command and `@` file menu is asked again after every deletion that removes text (Backspace, Delete, Ctrl+W/U/K) on the text before the cursor, so it follows `/exi` to `/ex` to `/` and closes when the `/` or `@` is gone; a cursor move alone opens nothing, and Esc closes it until the next edit.
- Pictures and files in a console message: `POST /api/uploads?name=` takes raw picture bytes (20 MiB, image `Content-Type`; the only non-JSON `/api` route), decides the type from the bytes, reads the sizes in the headers (every GIF frame, every HEIC image) and refuses over 120 MP before `sips` starts, scales PNG/JPEG to a long side of 1280 px, converts HEIC to JPEG and the first frame of GIF and WebP to PNG with `sips` (without it, 413 `picture_scale` or 415 `picture_convert`, never unscaled), strips EXIF, GPS, XMP, comments and text chunks from every picture it keeps (`picture_clean`), and keeps the picture in RAM (24 pictures, 64 MiB, 30 min) under an `id`. A turn names up to 4 in `images` and up to 8 text files (256 KiB each, 512 KiB in all) in `attachments`; text may be empty. The pictures are stored with the turn (`turn.started.images`, served by the blobs route) and sent as image parts. 400 `picture_gone`; 409 `model_text_only` when the model is known not to read pictures (also learned for a minute: a turn whose error says the model does not take pictures ends `provider_error` with `This model can't see pictures; choose one that can in Settings → Model`, and a retry is 409 `model_text_only`; a bare 400, a length error and a bad-picture error are not it), `chat_answering`; a picture cannot start a task. Drop, paste, the paperclip and `/attach` add them in the web console and the app; the terminal does not share this.
- Words added to a running turn: `POST /api/turns/{turn_id}/notes {text, images?, client_request_id?}` (202, `state` `sent` or `next`, `images` when it has pictures): the run reads them at its next step as the person's message (`inbox.accepted` names the note; session event `turn.note`); unread when the turn ends they run as the next turn, in order, and survive a restart; a Stop returns them in `unread_notes` of the cancel answer (pictures staged again under `images`). `images` are staged upload ids on the terms of a message's (at most 4, 400 `picture_gone`, 409 `model_text_only`); a picture needs no words (the model reads `[1 picture]`); the model gets them as image parts, or a line saying it cannot see them when it is known to read none. At most 20 per turn, 8,000 characters; text files cannot join; 409 `turn_not_running`, `not_your_turn`.
- Interactive `! COMMAND` (idle only): runs COMMAND in `$SHELL`/`/bin/sh` as the user in the workspace with the terminal handed over (Ctrl+C/Esc go to the child). Not a sandbox: no approval, checker or policy; it can leave the workspace. Output stays in the terminal: never in model context, history or events, and the command is not saved in input history. `/attach !` attaches a redacted snapshot (last 256 KiB, minus concealed text and anything before a screen clear, a cut start loses its partial first line) to the next message: it always prints the exact snapshot and asks `Attach this output?` (`Attach this redacted snapshot?` when redacted) as a list, `Attach it` or `Don't attach it`, starting on the latter, Esc does not attach; once attached it is stored with the session, unencrypted, like `/attach PATH`. `!` alone shows help; `\! text` sends a literal leading `! `. Refused (draft kept) during a turn, approval, switch or another command. melo exit sends SIGTERM, terminal hangup SIGHUP, then SIGKILL after 2 s, to the child's own process group only. Not in direct mode or the plain loop. See [terminal guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/terminal.md#run-a-shell-command).
- Terminal questions with fixed answers (first run, `melo setup`, `/attach !`) are arrow-key lists when stdin and stdout are TTYs and `TERM` is not `dumb`: no filter field, the safe or recommended row selected first, ↑↓ move, a number 1-9 chooses that row at once, Enter confirms, Esc takes the answer named in the key line (cancel the setup, decline), Ctrl+C exits 130, Ctrl+D exits 0. With stdin not a TTY the typed prompts are asked unchanged (`Use it? [Y/n]:`, `[r]etry, [s]ave anyway, [N]o [N]:`, a number for a backend), so scripted answers work. A direct run (a task, `--output-format json`) never asks. See [terminal guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/terminal.md#questions-are-lists).
- Terminal session tools: `/title [text]` shows/sets a title (kept until lazy first-turn creation); idle-only `/undo` forgets the newest finished turn, keeps typed history and never reverses file changes; a committed undo reports success even after Esc, and `/retry` re-runs that undone turn without undoing the previous one. `/usage` includes undone work, leaves missing/running counters unknown and reflows on narrow terminals; `/memory` inspects a copied, cleaned working window and explains the actual resume mode, without model calls or memory writes. `/copy [turn]` copies stored redacted Markdown without thinking, preserving indentation/newlines with bounded turn reads, not wrapped terminal output; local macOS uses bounded `/usr/bin/pbcopy`, SSH/other platforms/failure request OSC 52 (terminal support varies). Tests must fake native copying: temporary HOME does not isolate the OS clipboard.
- `/clear` (terminal chat) is `/new` on an empty screen: after the same reset it writes `ESC[H ESC[2J ESC[3J` (`TerminalOut.clear_screen`, queued with the text so the app is erased, the screen cleared and the welcome drawn in one pass) and draws the welcome again; `/new` keeps the page and prints the `New chat` rule. With `NO_COLOR`, `TERM=dumb` or output that is not a terminal `/clear` writes no escape code and prints the rule as `/new` does. Both are refused while a turn runs or files are staged.
- Terminal colours (interactive UI only; machine output unchanged): depth `NO_COLOR`/`TERM=dumb` → none, then `[cli] colors` (`-X cli.colors=16|256|truecolor`), `COLORTERM`, `TERM` `*256color`, else 16; background `[cli] background` (`-X cli.background=dark|light`), then an OSC 11/10 query (≤100 ms, DA1 sentinel, TTYs only), then `COLORFGBG`. Tool rows `<mark> <kind> <name>`: kinds `→` read, `±` write, `$` exec, `@` network (ASCII `> ~ $ @`); a nonzero `exit_code` draws `✗ … exit N` while the event stays `success`; the changed-files line marks `+` new, `~` modified. Fills (user band, code chips, code panel) need the exact background; else a `│` gutter and bold inline code. Panels and lists: approval frame in warn, title bold, chosen answer on the selection band, diff rows on ok/error bands; every list's chosen row on the band with one `❯`. Status bar zones `usage │ work │ run` (no model or folder; the mode always at the right with the key that switches it, `ask · shift+tab` / `auto · shift+tab` (` - ` in ASCII; Auto in the run colour and bold, Ask muted; the key goes below 60 columns, the mode stays; `⚠ YOLO: no approvals` has no key): local `↑ SENT ↓ RECEIVED · ctx USED/LIMIT ▮▯▯▯▯ · cache N% (avg N%) · idle Nm`; cloud `$COST` from `[pricing.<model>]` (input, output, cache_read per million tokens; tokens when a used model has no price) `· ctx … · limit N% ▮▮▯▯▯ ↻3m` from `x-ratelimit-*`/`anthropic-ratelimit-*` response headers; work (gateway tasks, polled every 5 s only while a gateway token exists) `2 running · 1 queued · P1 · ctrl+t tasks`; while a turn runs the run zone is `2/~8 · ctrl+o steps` (`~` learned from `run.progress` `expected_steps`/`past`; `step N` without a total), else the title; narrow drops the title, work details, usage details, the run key, then figures right to left; Ctrl+O lists the turn's steps; Ctrl+T lists the tasks and their actions (pause/resume, raise/lower priority, stop with a confirm) via `melo task`'s client. Welcome: a 5-row half-block head with ears from `support/gateway/static/moves/face-brand.png` at ≥256 colours, Unicode, ≥80 columns.
- Under an approval policy (terminal chat, console, saved tasks) each `shell_exec`/`python_exec`/`file_write` call is reviewed by fixed rules as routine, high-impact (installs, project restores, environments, large or outside downloads, downloaded code, writes/deletes outside the workspace, persistence, credentials, system settings, open services, sending files out, changes to localmelo) or undecided; a session grant covers routine calls only, high-impact and undecided calls ask every time (the console card and the terminal panel for a high-impact call give the reasons, offer Allow once and No/Deny only, and start on No/Deny; `pending_approvals[].review` = `{verdict, title, reasons}`), under a grant the chat's model first reviews an undecided call (runs on the grant only when it says routine and fits the request), terminal `auto` mode (`AutoPolicy`) asks nothing: routine runs, high is blocked unless the user's typed words ask for it (model `user_asked: yes`; never with parts the rules could not read), undecided runs only when the model finds it routine and fitting (a step that goes by the exit status of a pipeline without `pipefail`, as `pytest | tail && git commit` or Python reading the `.returncode` of such a command, is undecided with a reason that says the status is the last command's), a write of code is judged by what it writes, a test or build runner is undecided after code in the folder changed in the chat, a tool the rules do not read is undecided, a block's tool result tells the agent to explain and not to retry another way, and a second block of the same kind ends the run `completed` with the explanation; `tool.finished.approval` adds `mode`, `review`, `step_key`, `allowance`, and `run.finished.reviews` lists the blocks; a change to the running localmelo (its import folder or app bundle, and `~/.cache/localmelo`) is denied without asking. Direct, `--brief` and `--yolo` runs are not reviewed.
- Approval cards start with one plain sentence (#454): `review.gist` in `tool.finished.approval` and a top-level `gist` in `pending_approvals[]` = `{say: {id, params}, by: "model"|"code", warn?: {id, params}, note?, apps?: [names]}` (catalog ids `gist.say.<id>`, `gist.warn.<id>`; a param may be another `{id, params}` sentence, as in `then` and `more`, or a list of names; `null` for browser sites). The main chat's waiting card says it too (`Needs your OK: <sentence>`, with the warning). For a command or script melo builds `say` from the call and names every effect in order (`Operate Safari, then delete files`; a long command ends `and N more`). The model's own words are only a `why` argument of `python_exec`/`shell_exec` (or another tool) or the leading comment of their code (`shell_exec` and `python_exec` take an optional `why`, one short sentence in the person's language, at most 120 characters shown; it changes nothing about what runs, how the step is reviewed, or when a step counts as repeated), always labelled `melo says: …`: they are `say` (`by: "model"`) only when the review found nothing, and `note` below the code-built `say` otherwise. If the words disagree with the code about deleting files or sending data out, `warn` quotes them (`delete`, `send_out`; `delete_target`, `send_out_target` with a `target` param listing the places the code acts on that the words do not name, when the effect is right but the words name files, folders or hosts and some place of the code is not among them, compared by name, never when the words name none; the git words "revert", "restore", "undo"… cover only a step that is nothing but checkout, restore, switch or stash discards, never `git clean` or `reset --hard`); the sentence never changes the verdict, category or reasons. A script that operates one app by its plain name (`osascript` `tell application "Safari"` with plain verbs, `open -a Notes`) is the high-impact kind `app_control` ("Control an app?"; an allow-list, `RULES_VERSION` 3); it is click-only like `system` (never allowed by the user's words or the model's review, never by a session grant; Auto blocks it, only Allow once runs it), and every other script, a shell through AppleScript, keys, System Events, a terminal, a path, a second app, `shortcuts run`, a script that reaches macOS without naming an app (`use framework`, `current application`, `load script`, a `|name|` identifier, any JXA other than the plain one-liner), an `open` of a link that is not http, https or file (`open shortcuts://…`), erasing a disk (`diskutil eraseDisk`), and stopping other programs (`pkill` with any option, `killall`, `kill` of a process the step did not start, psutil `kill`), stays `system`; options count only before the first target (an option's value is never read as an option), a name counts as a started process only if it only ever holds `$!` in the step's own shell (a `read`, loop, `(( … ))`, `let`, `unset`, `source`, `eval`, name reference, pipeline, or any other write of the name, such as `printf -vNAME`, `arr[NAME=5]=1` (a bracket expression over 200 characters takes every name out), `declare -i` or a name built by an expansion, takes it out), and program names in any letter case, commands inside loops and conditions, backquoted commands, the `$(…)` and backquotes of a here-document whose delimiter is not quoted, and `bash -c -l '…'` are read; a `$'…'` quote, a backquote that never closes, a here-document that is not a plain `<<WORD` (`<<-`, a partly quoted or escaped word, two on a line, no closing line, a `<<` shift), a `$(…)` that cannot be balanced exactly, has a `case` in it, or has quotes the lexer pairs differently from the shell (read from the text itself and reviewed as its own command when it has a quote, a backslash or a `case`) and a command or code over 256 KB (`MAX_TEXT`) are undecided (the text is cut into words by `melo.contracts.shell_lexer`, `shlex`'s tokenizer with linear accumulation, so a long word costs time in proportion to its length; a test keeps it equal to `shlex` token for token); discarding uncommitted work (`git checkout -- .`, `git restore`, `git reset --hard`, `git clean`, `git stash drop`) is `delete`.
- Folders outside the workspace (#405): in a chat or task the person started, a file tool's path outside the workspace asks (card, terminal list: Allow once / Allow this folder for this chat / Always allow this folder, kept in `[workspace] extra_folders` / Deny) instead of `Path '<path>' is outside allowed workspace root`; a write outside asks every time and is never granted; keys, `~/.cache/localmelo`, system folders and the whole home folder are never offered, nor is a macOS alias such as `/.vol`, and paths are compared as the file system names them (letter case, aliases) and opened only as checked; `file_write`/`file_edit` refuse a file with another name (a hard link), as does a read outside the workspace, and the review counts a hard link to a file outside the workspace as a change to that file; Auto never decides it; a run with no one to ask (direct, `--yolo`, deny mode, tasks the person did not start) refuses as before. [Tools guide](https://localmelo.github.io/localmelo/guides/tools-mcp.md#folders-outside-the-workspace).
- Grants (`support/sessions/grants.py`, `routes_grants.py`, `support/cli/grants.py`): every "allow ... for this chat" (a tool, a site to open/read or click and choose on, a folder outside the workspace to read, another app's window) is a row of the `grants` table in a sessions file (component `grants`, version 1; gateway `~/.cache/localmelo/gateway/sessions.db`, the terminal's own chat `~/.cache/localmelo/cli/sessions.db`) and survives a restart. Columns `id, session_id, session_kind, scope, kind, key, label, target, decided_by, granted_at, request_id, revoked_at`; a revoke sets `revoked_at`, revoked rows go after the store's thinking retention (30 days), a session's rows go with it (`ON DELETE CASCADE`); no config key. What the person allows in the main chat (`scope` `global`) counts everywhere (every side chat, the tasks they start, the terminal; the terminal's own chat reads it at every check, so a gateway revoke holds in a running turn's next step; an unreadable or newer-version file gives none); a side chat's, the terminal's own chat's and a task's grant (`scope` `session`) holds there only; what Auto keeps (a site read, `decided_by` `auto`) holds in that chat only, even the main chat. A row that breaks a rule is ignored when read. Never kept, never listed: Allow once, typing, sending a form, a click on a password/code/card field, a consent control or a box from another site, a press in another app's window, paying, changing an account's settings, every high-impact step. `GET /api/grants` -> `{"grants": [{id, scope, session_id, session_kind (main|side|task|terminal), chat_title, kind (tool|site|folder|window), key, label, action (tool|open|act|read|folder|window), target, by (person|auto), granted_at}]}`, `global` first then chat by chat, newest first (the order Settings → Permissions and `/grants` number); `DELETE /api/grants/{id}` -> 204, 404 `not_found` for an unknown or revoked id, at once for running chats; both behind the usual token and origin guard. `GET /api/sessions/{id}` `grants`/`granted_at` list what holds in the chat, open or not (a side chat's include the main chat's); `grants_everywhere` names a side chat's grants that came from the main chat; `DELETE /api/sessions/{id}/grants/{name}` takes back the chat's own grant and a `global` one (everywhere) -> 200 `{revoked: [{key, scope}], everywhere}`, `DELETE .../grants` the chat's own (main chat: every `global`) -> 200 `{revoked, still_everywhere}`, 503 when the store cannot save a revoke, `DELETE .../folders?path=` works for a chat that is not open. `/approvals forget NAME` in a side chat on a main-chat grant takes it back everywhere; in the terminal's own chat it says the grant is the main chat's. The main chat's own cards and terminal list say a kept answer counts in every chat. Deleting a chat deletes its grants; moving a side chat takes back its own; the terminal's own chat's `/new`/`/clear` start with none of the last chat's, a resume brings them back. Tool authors: `TOOL_ASK.get().granted(name)` (`melo.contracts.approvals.holds_grant(policy, name)`); never true for a question that asks every time.
- Auto asks instead of blocking (#465): in a chat (console, app, terminal) and in a task the person started, a step Auto's review stops whose every category a person may allow (install, restore, env, download, outside_write, delete, send_out, service, beyond_request, opaque, and the card-only money and account) waits on the usual approval card (`pending_approvals`, terminal list): Allow once, Deny with a note (the model reads `The user chose Don't allow for this step, …`; the same step or one alike is refused unasked for the rest of the run, `declined: true`), and for a `browser:`/`browser-act:` site stopped only as `beyond_request`, `session` (`offers_chat: true`): a grant of that site question for the chat, which covers the same kind of step on that site in later messages; typing, form sends and high-impact steps never ride it. Grants are listed in `GET /api/sessions/{id}` `grants`, in the Ask/Auto chip's menu with Remove (`DELETE /api/sessions/{id}/grants/{name}`, slashes allowed), in Settings → Permissions and `/grants` (`GET /api/grants`) and, in the terminal's own chat, in `/approvals` (`/approvals forget SITE`). Other categories (credentials, system, app_control, persistence, remote_code, unreviewed, self) and runs with nobody to ask (chores, other-origin tasks, a bare `AutoPolicy()`) keep the block. Auto asks only while someone watches: a gateway chat or task needs an open `GET /api/sessions/{id}/events?watch=true` stream of it (or of the task's chat), which the console, the app and the terminal send; a script that follows without `watch` gets the block at once, and the terminal's own chat asks only on a TTY. `[approvals] auto_asks = false` (developer setting, `-X approvals.auto_asks=false`) never asks: blocks as before. A card unanswered for 1 minute (`AUTO_ASK_WAIT_S`), or whose last viewer is gone for 5 s, is declined: `approval.resolved` `denied`/`timeout`, the model reads `The user did not answer the card for this step (…), so it counts as Don't allow …`, and the step is not asked again that run. After a reload the review's window takes the person's typed words of the chat's newest 2 earlier turns (never answers, task questions, page text or recalled notes); the review prompt counts any recent request and a named box or button.
- Auto's goal (#465): a step the review finds on the goal of the chat (`fits_request: yes`) with no high-impact category (`none`, `beyond_request`) runs, whatever the latest words name; the person's words only ever add. Site questions that carry no value (`access` `act`/`point`/`dialog`: a click, a choice, a point, an OK to a box) never count as `credentials` unless `holds_secret` (melo's secret detectors) finds one in the step (a sign-in or quick-login click is judged on the goal); a read (its address can hold a key), a search, typed text, a form and gate steps keep it. New card-only categories `money` and `account` always ask (the card when watched, else a block), even when asked for, and never ride a grant. A goal review reads the person's older messages of the chat (the first kept, then the newest; `CHAT_REQUESTS` = 6) and the recalled notes of the message as `<recalled>` (they count only where the words point to them); consents read the 3 newest only. The browser's click, choice and typing questions carry `on` (`a button "Check in"`), reviewed per target, also on a site the words name (a read of a named site stays routine). A control in another site's box known by name, or a frame with a title, is clicked on the act question; a frame melo cannot tell asks `browser-point:` with `target: "unknown"` (Auto: `opaque`, the card, no review). A Don't allow of one named button declines only it for the turn. A site read Auto let run (`browser:` only, a plain address, no `money`/`account`) stays allowed for the chat in Ask too (`RememberingPolicy.passed_in_auto`, origin `session`, listed in `grants`, Remove works), never covering a step Auto stops; a click never stays allowed this way: Ask asks about every click. `REVIEWS_PER_TURN` = 12 (was 6). Review prompt 3011 -> 3789 chars; chat identity +296 chars (`APPROVALS_RULE`: melo asks on a card, never ask for a typed permission, a recalled reply that refused or said a step was blocked is no precedent, report only what a step result shows). A blocked note adds `Never ask the user to type a permission …`, and for a card kind blocked with nobody to ask, `ALLOW_WHEN_OPEN`.
- melo acts for the user, in their name (`support/sessions/identity.py` `ACTING_RULE`, `ACTING_NOTE`; `support/gateway/console/front.py` `FRONT_TEXT`; `support/gateway/workers.py` `WORKER_GUIDE`): the model does what the user asks or authorizes (apply with their resume, sign in, fill in and submit a form, send a message as them, book) and does not refuse, hedge or lecture because a step speaks for the user or cannot be undone; the approval cards (Ask) and Auto's review decide which steps the user confirms. Only what would harm other people is declined. `ACTING_RULE` is in every chat's identity and at the end of `WORKER_GUIDE`; `ACTING_NOTE`, a one-line reminder, follows the user's message in the main chat and the side chats. `IDENTITY_TEXT` says the cards ask, not the model. `front_rules.authorizes` ("I authorize you to apply", "我授权你去投简历") makes `start_rule` read a go-ahead as a request.
- Ask or Auto per console chat: `sessions.meta.approvals` (`approvals` on every session object, with `allowances`), switched by `PATCH /api/sessions/{id} {"approvals": "auto"}` from the chat's next step (a waiting card stays) or set by `POST /api/sessions {"approvals": …}`; new chats start in `[approvals] mode` (`ask` default; Settings `approvals`, `-X approvals.mode=auto`; also the terminal's own chat), and the main chat follows it until set.
